findings.title: A deleted POP message comes back in the reopened conversation
findings.what_this_is: After a command chosen inside an opened conversation, open_conversation_again reopens the window right away. It builds the list from the rows the main window holds (conversation_nodes).
findings.problem: For mail kept only on this computer (POP, or a folder on this computer), Delete does not take the row out at once. delete_if_local sends MessageLeftTheFolder through the runtime, and that update is only handled on the next timer tick. The window reopens before that tick, so it still lists the deleted message and puts the cursor on it.
findings.concrete_case: POP account, conversation view. Open a conversation of three messages and press Delete on one. The window comes back still listing it. The person presses Delete again. The message is now in the local Trash, so local_folders::deleting answers RemoveFromThisComputer and take_off_this_computer erases it. There is no question first and no other copy.
findings.fix: In delete_these, in the DeletedHere::Left arm, call take_row_out_of_the_list(state, list, cache, message.row_id) and the_folder_counts_moved(state, tx) straight away, the way complete_here_then_tell_the_server does. Then remove the rt.spawn that sends MessageLeftTheFolder from delete_if_local, which leaves the MessageLeftTheFolder variant and its arm unused, so delete them too.
findings.if_we_skip: POP users can lose mail for good. The window tells them a message they deleted is still there, and the second Delete erases it.
findings.evidence: I read the file with git show 0b781473:src/presentation/wx_app.rs. L29936-29957: run(command), then `let now = conversation_nodes(...)`, then where_the_cursor_comes_back(&nodes, message, &now), with no event loop in between. L28344-28351: delete_if_local does `rt.spawn(async move { tx_now.send(UIUpdate::MessageLeftTheFolder(row_id)).await })`. L25181-25188: only that arm calls take_row_out_of_the_list for this path. L26865: the server path removes the row synchronously. git show 0b781473:src/presentation/wx_thread_view.rs L227-243: where_the_cursor_comes_back keeps the same message 'while it is still listed'. git show 0b781473:src/application/local_folders.rs L302-309: Delete in the local Trash means RemoveFromThisComputer. git show 0b781473:src/application/local_delete.rs L82-89: that branch calls take_off_this_computer.
checker_notes:
STANDS: The bug happens at 0b781473. Delete inside an opened conversation reaches the Act arm (wx_app.rs L29930-29974). That arm calls the main dispatch, which runs synchronously, through the Delete arm (L5770) into delete_these and then delete_if_local. For mail kept on this computer, delete_if_local moves the message to the local Trash in the cache. It does not take the row out of state.messages. Instead it uses rt.spawn to send MessageLeftTheFolder (L28346-28351). That update is only read by `ui_rx.try_recv()` in the timer tick (L6585), and the event loop does not run between `run(command)` and `conversation_nodes(...)` (L29950). So `now` still holds the deleted message. where_the_cursor_comes_back (wx_thread_view.rs) keeps the cursor on it "while it is still listed", and show_thread_dialog builds its tree once from those nodes.

On the second Delete in the reopened window, nothing stops it:
- the_named_message (L12632) falls back to `cache.get_message`, which still finds the message, now in Trash.
- deleting_asks returns None, because a named message has no conversations, so no question is asked.
- owner_of falls back to the active account.
- local_folders::deleting answers RemoveFromThisComputer, because the message is already in the local Trash and `trash != from` is false.
- local_delete::perform then calls take_off_this_computer, and the copy that could have been recovered is gone.

The Act arm and where_the_cursor_comes_back are new in 13.2, since neither appears at 2a4679a9. The delayed MessageLeftTheFolder path is older, so 13.2 introduced the combination. The proposed fix holds up: delete_if_local has one caller (delete_these), and MessageLeftTheFolder has one sender.

STANDS: The finding holds at 0b781473. Nothing at the head commit handles it: no code, no test, no shortcut comment, no changelog line and no ledger entry. I searched WINDOWS.md and the 13.2-03 plan and summaries for MessageLeftTheFolder, POP, "on this computer" and the conversation window. Ledger rows 839 to 841 cover the IMAP behaviour only.

How it happens:
- delete_these (L27550) calls delete_if_local, its only caller. For mail kept on this computer, delete_if_local takes the row out later: it only queues UIUpdate::MessageLeftTheFolder through rt.spawn (L28346-28351).
- Only the timer tick drains those updates (L6585). The other try_recv loops are in tests.
- The Act arm (L29930-29974) runs the command, then at once rebuilds the list with conversation_nodes from s.messages (L16672). The row is still in s.messages, so where_the_cursor_comes_back keeps the cursor on the deleted message (wx_thread_view L227-243).
- show_thread_dialog is modal with fixed nodes (L467), so a tick while it is open does not change what it lists.
- The IMAP path removes the row at once (L26865), which is why only mail on this computer is hit.

The second Delete:
- acting_on still names the message, and the_named_message falls back to the cache (L12647-12653), so the message is found even after the tick removed the row.
- deleting_asks returns None for one named message, so no question is asked.
- local_delete::perform finds the message now in the local Trash. local_folders::deleting answers RemoveFromThisComputer when trash == from (L302-309), and take_off_this_computer erases it (local_delete L82-89).
- allow_deleting_here defaults to true (account.rs L203), so this happens with default settings.
- The bug comes from 13.2: the reopen after a command was added in 13.2-03.

The fix works. delete_these already has cache_for_deleting and list in hand. take_row_out_of_the_list handles a set and conversation view the same way the server path uses it.

One correction to the fix: deleting the MessageLeftTheFolder arm breaks tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs. That test lists the arm's first line as a place that moves a folder count (L68), so that entry must be changed to the new site in the same commit. No guard record names the arm.

STANDS: I checked this at 0b781473 and it holds.

1. The Act arm (wx_app.rs L29930-29974) runs the command through `runs_a_command`. That is the main window's dispatch, called directly in the same call (L6375, L6331). Then it reads `conversation_nodes`, which builds the list from `s.messages` (L16672-16682), with no event loop in between.
2. A local delete removes no row in that call. `delete_if_local` (L28344-28351) only spawns a send of `MessageLeftTheFolder`. That update is handled only when the timer ticks and calls `ui_rx.try_recv` (L6585). The server path removes its row at once (L26865).
3. So the reopened window still lists the deleted message. `where_the_cursor_comes_back` keeps the cursor on that same message because it is "still listed" (wx_thread_view.rs L227-243).
4. A second Delete on it is not stopped:
   - The update has arrived by then, so the row is gone from `s.messages`.
   - `the_named_message` falls back to `cache.get_message` (L12638-12653), which finds the row by id in any folder.
   - `what_the_command_is_for` returns one message with no conversations, so `deleting_asks` returns None and no question is shown.
   - `local_delete::perform` now finds the message in the local Trash. `local_folders::deleting` (L302-308) answers RemoveFromThisComputer, and `take_off_this_computer` erases it.

This needs the account's "Let me delete mail on this computer" setting to be on, but that is how a POP user deletes at all. The window says nothing when it reopens after a command, so the person hears the deleted message under the cursor and is likely to press Delete again. Losing the only copy without a question is data loss, so "must" is honest. Scale does not matter here: it happens with one conversation of three messages.

The fix is right and small: call `take_row_out_of_the_list` and `the_folder_counts_moved` straight away in the `DeletedHere::Left` arm, as `complete_here_then_tell_the_server` does. One thing the finding misses: deleting the `MessageLeftTheFolder` variant and its arm also means changing `tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs`. Its `THE_PLACES_THAT_CHANGE_A_COUNT` list searches the window's source for the line `"UIUpdate::MessageLeftTheFolder(cache_id) => {"`. If that line is gone, the test reports that it "reads nothing", so the list must point at `delete_these` instead. Guard records anchored on that line would need re-measuring too.

STANDS: I traced the path at 0b781473 and both halves happen.

First Delete: in the Act arm (wx_app.rs L29930), `run(ID_DELETE)` goes through `chosen_messages`, then `the_named_message` (the message is still in `s.messages`). `deleting_asks` returns None for one named message, so no dialog opens. Then `delete_these` calls `delete_if_local` (L28341). For a POP Inbox, `local_delete::perform` returns `MoveTo(trash)`. `move_message` runs, and the row is taken off the list only through `rt.spawn(... MessageLeftTheFolder ...)` (L28346-28351). That update is drained only by the timer tick (`ui_rx.try_recv`, L6584), and nothing in the Act arm gives the event loop a turn. So `conversation_nodes` (L29950, reads `s.messages` only) still lists message 2. `where_the_cursor_comes_back` finds it still listed and returns 2. The modal tree is rebuilt with message 2 under the cursor. The server path does not have this problem: it calls `take_row_out_of_the_list` synchronously (L26865).

Second Delete: the tick runs 20 times a second, also inside the modal dialog, so within about 50 ms it removes row 2 from `s.messages`. The tree still shows the node, because it is built once from `nodes`. Delete on it gives `act_on_the_message`, which returns `Act{ID_DELETE, 2}`. Then `the_named_message` falls back to `cache.get_message(2)`, which has no folder or deleted filter, so it finds the copy in Trash. `deleting_asks` is None again. `owner_of` cannot find the row, so it falls back to `active_account_id`, which the folder tree set to the POP account at L3432. `perform` then calls `local_folders::deleting(trash_path, POP, ToTrash, true)`, and trash == from, so it answers `RemoveFromThisComputer`. `take_off_this_computer` deletes the row, writes back only the kept columns with secure overwrite on, and the body is gone. No question is asked, and Undo cannot bring back the text.

The finding reproduces as stated.

STANDS: I confirmed the bug at 0b781473 and found nothing that already covers it.

1. **The deleted message comes back.** The conversation window's Act arm (wx_app.rs L29930-29975) runs the Delete command through `runs_a_command` straight away, on the same thread (L6331, L6375). It then reads `conversation_nodes` (L29950), which looks only at `s.messages` (L16672-16712). For mail kept on this computer, `delete_if_local` does not take the row out at once. It sends `MessageLeftTheFolder` through `rt.spawn` (L28346-28351), and that message is only acted on later, when the window's timer runs (L6584-6609, then L25181-25188). Nothing between the command and the re-read lets that timer run. `show_thread_dialog` gets a fixed list and never reads the state again. So the window reopens still listing the deleted message. The cursor also lands on it, because `where_the_cursor_comes_back` checks the acted-on message first and finds it still listed. Mail on a server is different: `complete_here_then_tell_the_server` takes the row out at once (L26865).

2. **A second Delete removes the only copy.** By the second press the timer has dropped the row. `the_named_message` (L12632-12654) then reads the message from the store, where it now sits in the local Trash. `what_the_command_is_for` returns that one message, so `deleting_asks` asks nothing. `owner_of` falls back to the open account. `local_folders::deleting` sees that the Trash is where the message already is and answers `RemoveFromThisComputer`. `take_off_this_computer` then deletes the only copy, with no question.

3. **POP mail really gets conversations.** `upsert_message` gives it a conversation id from its own headers, and `apply_threading` groups any folder's messages. So POP accounts do reach this path.

**Nothing at the head covers it:**
- No ledger row in .planning/WINDOWS.md. Rows 839 and 841 cover only Pratik's IMAP Inbox.
- No test. `tests/the_conversation_window_acts_on_the_message_under_its_cursor.rs` drives the dialog alone and has no local delete.
- No `shortcut:` or `ponytail:` comment.
- The 13.2-03 plans never mention POP or `delete_if_local`.
- The changelog's LIST-05 entry is wrong for this mail. It promises that the conversation "comes back by itself, listing what is true now, with the cursor ... on the one after it when that message has gone."

**The proposed fix is safe.** Taking the row out at once in `delete_these` on `Left` is what the server path already does. Two things would need updating with it: the source-reading test `tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs:68`, and the source-reading tests that name `delete_if_local` (`tests/wired.rs:3791`, `tests/each_set_command_has_a_quiet_do_half.rs:174`). Those are upkeep, not a sign the fix is wrong.

STANDS: The finding holds at 0b781473. In the conversation window's Act arm (wx_app.rs about L29930-29975), the Delete runs `dispatch` straight away, then reads `now` from `s.messages`. Nothing in between drains the update channel; only the timer at L6585 does. For mail kept on this computer, `delete_these` goes to `delete_if_local` (its only caller, L27550). That function only queues `MessageLeftTheFolder` with `rt.spawn` (L28344-28351), so the row is still in `s.messages`. Because the message is still listed, `where_the_cursor_comes_back` puts the cursor back on it, and the window reopens on the deleted message. Server mail behaves differently: `complete_here_then_tell_the_server` removes its row at once with `take_row_out_of_the_list`.

The second press really does destroy the message. `local_delete::perform` used `move_message`, which keeps the same row id. So `the_named_message` finds the message in the store, or still in the rows if the timer has not run yet. `folder_path_for_message` now answers the Trash, and `local_folders::deleting` returns RemoveFromThisComputer because from equals trash. `deleting_asks` asks nothing for one named message. `take_off_this_computer` then runs `DELETE FROM messages` in a transaction. `remember_the_last_action` also replaces the first delete's undo entry, so Undo cannot bring it back.

Neither docs/changelog.md nor .planning/WINDOWS.md mentions this as a known limitation. It is reachable at the expected load: one person with a POP or Local Folders account in conversation view, and allow_deleting_here is on by default. "must" is the right group: the first press gives a wrong result in an area the owner reported as broken, and the natural second press loses mail.

The proposed fix is sound and close to the smallest. In `delete_these`, on `DeletedHere::Left`, call `take_row_out_of_the_list(state, list, &cache_for_deleting, message.row_id)` and `the_folder_counts_moved`, as the server path does. Then delete the `rt.spawn` in `delete_if_local`. `delete_if_local` is the only sender of `MessageLeftTheFolder` (git grep), so that variant and its handler arm (L25181) can be deleted as well. The extra change to make `the_named_message` refuse rows that are not loaded is a separate safety net, not needed to fix this case.

duplicate_reports.title: A message deleted on this computer comes back in the conversation window
duplicate_reports.problem: Mail kept only on this computer (any POP account, Local Folders) does not leave the loaded rows when Delete runs. `delete_if_local` moves it to the local Trash and then sends `MessageLeftTheFolder` through the runtime. That update is only handled on a later timer tick. The Act arm reads `now` before that tick, so the window comes back still listing the deleted message, with the cursor on it. Mail on a server is different: `complete_here_then_tell_the_server` removes its row at once (L26865), which is the path 13.2-03 was built and tested against.
duplicate_reports.concrete_case: A POP account with Delete allowed (the default), conversation view, a conversation of 3 in Inbox. Open it, arrow to message 2, press Delete. The window comes back and the screen reader reads message 2 again, as if Delete did nothing. The person presses Delete again. By now the tick has dropped the row, so `the_named_message` falls back to the store and finds the message in the local Trash. `delete_these` -> `local_delete::perform` -> `local_folders::deleting(trash, .., ToTrash, true)` answers `RemoveFromThisComputer` because trash == from. `deleting_asks` asks nothing for one named message. The only copy is taken off the computer with no question.
duplicate_reports.fix: In `delete_these`, on `DeletedHere::Left`, take the row out at once with `take_row_out_of_the_list(state, list, cache, message.row_id)` and call `the_folder_counts_moved`, as the server path does. Then delete the `rt.spawn(... MessageLeftTheFolder ...)` block in `delete_if_local`. Also make `the_named_message` refuse a message that is no longer in the loaded rows, instead of reading it from the store. Its own doc says the tree is built from those rows, so the store branch only ever runs for a stale row.

findings.title: Folder counts stop updating when the tree was drawn for another account
findings.what_this_is: After a mark, delete or move made here, say_the_folder_counts_again (13.2-31.2) reads the folder tree again. It rewords only the rows whose text changed, and it does that only when both readings hold exactly the same rows in the same order.
findings.problem: The fresh reading uses the active account (folder_tree_updates(cache, active_account_id)). The tree on screen, though, was drawn by whichever account's check ran last, since every check calls folder_tree_updates(&cache, &account.id). The Labels branch belongs to one account. When the two accounts have different labels, rows_that_read_differently returns None. The function then only writes a log line, and no count changes.
findings.concrete_case: Two accounts: Work has a label and Home has none. The background check of Work ran last, so the tree shows Work's Labels branch. The person arrows into Home's Inbox, which sets active_account_id without a rebuild, and presses M on an unread message. Home's Inbox in the tree keeps the old unread count until the next check.
findings.fix: Pair the rows by identity instead of requiring identical lists. For each held row (index i), find the fresh row with the same identity. If its label differs, call set_item_text on item i and update the held row's label in place. This removes the give-up branch, so a Labels branch that differs no longer blocks the folder counts.
findings.if_we_skip: The 'counts change at once' fix does nothing for many people with two or more accounts, and the only trace is an info line in the log.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/presentation/wx_app.rs. L21443-21447: looked_at = active_account_id, then folder_tree_updates(cache, &looked_at). L21461-21464: the None case is logged and returns. L14743: labels = cache.get_tags_for_account(account_id). L32313, L28900, L9705: checks redraw the tree with each checked account's own id. L3412-3438: arrowing into another account's folder sets active_account_id with 'The tree is not read back'. git show 0b781473:src/presentation/folder_tree.rs L681-690: the Labels rows exist only when labels is not empty. L959-972: rows_that_read_differently needs the same length and the same identities. git grep shows tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs has no label or second-account case.
checker_notes: STANDS: I followed the path at 0b781473 and the bug happens as described. (1) folder_tree_updates (wx_app.rs:14743) reads the Labels branch for one account only, through get_tags_for_account, which runs `WHERE account_id = ?1` (tags.rs:107). folder_tree::rows adds the Labels rows only when that list is not empty (folder_tree.rs:681-691). A label's row identity is WhichRow::Label(id), and every label has its own id. (2) Each background check redraws the tree with the account it just checked: spawn_mail_sync at :32313 and check_pop_mail at :28900. F9 and the start check go through every enabled account "in list order" (:28985-29005). An IDLE watch waking checks only the account that woke (:25259-25266). The FoldersLoaded arm (:23876-23891) stores whatever rows arrive in tree_rows and never checks whose labels they are. (3) Arrowing onto another account's folder sets active_account_id and does not rebuild the tree (:3412-3433). Tests at :40224 and :40231 make sure the selection handler never rebuilds it. (4) M goes to write_flags_or_put_the_row_back (:23775), then the_folder_counts_moved, then the FolderCountsMoved arm (:23928), then say_the_folder_counts_again. That function reads the tree fresh for active_account_id, which is Home (:21443-21447). The fresh reading has no Labels rows, but the held rows still have Work's Labels heading and its label rows. So the lengths differ and rows_that_read_differently returns None (folder_tree.rs:959-964). The function writes an info line to the log and returns (:21461-21463). Home Inbox's unread count on screen stays old until the next rebuild, and that rebuild may again use Work's labels. Two accounts with labels give the same result, because their label ids never match. Nothing ledgers this. The doc comment says only that rows which "came, went or moved since it was drawn" wait. The 13.2-31.2 plan (section 9) lists labels among what is read but never mentions the account mismatch. tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs has no case with a second account or with labels. The proposed fix, pairing rows by identity, is sound because the held rows match the items on screen position for position. One limit: this is a stale count on screen, not data loss, and before 13.2 the count also waited for the next sync. Still, it is a wrong result in the new fix for a regression the owner reported, so it is a bug.

STANDS: I could not refute it. The bug happens at 0b781473 and nothing covers it. (1) folder_tree_updates (wx_app.rs:14721) builds the Labels branch from one account only: cache.get_tags_for_account(account_id) at :14743, and tags.rs:107 filters on account_id. (2) spawn_mail_sync goes through every account it was given and redraws the tree for each one with that account's id (:32313). The FoldersLoaded arm (:23876) rebuilds the tree whatever account the rows came from. So after F9, the start-up check or a scheduled check, the tree shows the Labels of whichever account was checked last. (3) Moving into another account's folder sets active_account_id and does not redraw the tree (:3412-3438, and the test at :40228 makes sure it never does). At start-up active_account_id is the first account (:1088), while the start-up check draws the tree for the last. (4) say_the_folder_counts_again (:21443-21464) reads the tree again for active_account_id. rows_that_read_differently (folder_tree.rs:959) answers None when the two readings differ in length or identity, and the function then only logs. Concrete case: Work has a label and Home has none, and Work was checked last. M in Home's Inbox reads a tree with no Labels rows against a held tree that has them, so the lengths differ, nothing is reworded, and the count stays old until the next check. This also happens from the very start of a session, whenever the first account's labels differ from the last account's. Already handled? No. The doc comment only names rows that came, went or moved since the tree was drawn. This case is different: the screen did not change, the fresh reading is for another account. Ledger 836 is marked fixed and ledger 899 is only the listening check. No ledger row mentions labels from the wrong account. The changelog entry (line 1582) says the count "changes at once" and lists no multi-account limit. The 13.2-31.2 plan chose active_account_id without thinking about this. tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs uses only acct-1 and has no labels. The proposed fix is safe if it is written as described: pair each held row with the fresh row of the same identity, reword item i, update the held row's label in place, and compare the item count with held.len(), not fresh.len(). The three unit tests on rows_that_read_differently that expect None (folder_tree.rs:1435-1473) would need rewriting, but nothing the person uses breaks. A smaller fix would be to read with the account that last drew the tree, but the window does not keep that today. Severity: the counts on screen go stale, no data is lost, but the 13.2 fix silently fails for anyone with two or more accounts and labels in only some of them. That makes it a bug at the expected load, so "must".

STANDS: The finding holds at 0b781473. I could not refute it.

- **The fresh reading uses the wrong account.** `say_the_folder_counts_again` (wx_app.rs:21438) re-reads the tree with `folder_tree_updates(cache, active_account_id)`.
- **The Labels branch belongs to one account.** In `folder_tree_updates`, the labels come from `get_tags_for_account(account_id)` (14743), and `folder_tree::rows` adds the Labels rows only when that list is not empty (folder_tree.rs:681-690).
- **The tree on screen can be another account's.** Every `FoldersLoaded` redraws the tree with no account filter (23876-23891). Each account's pass in `spawn_mail_sync` sends one, read with that account's id (32313), and the starting `load_module_data` draws with the open account.
- **Arrowing into another account does not redraw.** The selection handler sets `active_account_id` from the row and does not read the tree back (3412-3433). `test_landing_on_a_row_does_not_read_the_tree_back` makes sure of that.
- **Two accounts never share a label.** Label ids are the primary key of the `tags` table (mod.rs:1993), so two accounts always have different `Label(id)` rows. That holds even when both have the starting five labels, whose ids are `{account}:{keyword}`.
- **Result: the give-up branch runs.** `rows_that_read_differently` needs the same length and the same identities, so it returns `None`. The function then writes an info line to the log and changes nothing.

**Concrete case, simpler than the reviewer's, with no check needed.** Two accounts, and labels exist in only one: Work has the starting five, made the first time a label or Quick Step is used there, and Home has none. Start the app in Work, so the tree is drawn with Work's labels. Arrow into Home's Inbox and press M. The fresh reading for Home has no Labels branch, so the lengths differ, and Home's Inbox keeps its old unread count until the next check. If both accounts have labels, the label ids still differ, so it fails the same way.

**Tests.** `tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs` uses only `acct-1` and has no labels. The three `rows_that_read_differently` cases in folder_tree.rs do not cover this either.

**Scale.** One person with a few accounts is exactly where this happens, and the owner asked for this fix by name ("is confusing"). It is not a regression: before 13.2 the counts also waited for the next check. But the delivered feature silently does nothing for any person with two or more accounts who has used labels. That is a wrong result, so "must" (bug) fits the given groups. If anything, it sits at the light end of must, because nothing is lost and the next check corrects the count.

**Fix.** Pairing rows by identity is smaller than the other options:
- Each held row with a fresh row of the same identity and a different label gets `set_item_text` at its own position, and its held label is updated in place.
- The item-count check compares against `held.len()` instead of `fresh.len()`.
- The `None` branch goes away, which deletes code.

The other options are bigger. Storing which account drew the tree needs a new state field and a change to `FoldersLoaded` and its callers. Filtering out the label rows breaks the pairing between positions and items.

STANDS: The bug reproduces at 0b781473. These are the steps.

1. spawn_mail_sync (L31962 loop, L32313) calls folder_tree_updates(&cache, &account.id) for every account it checks. That covers F9 and the check at start, which take every enabled account, and a watch waking for one account.
2. The FoldersLoaded arm (L23876-23892) sets s.tree_rows = rows. Nothing ties those rows to the active account. So the tree on screen holds the labels of whichever account was drawn last.
3. Arrowing into another account's folder sets s.active_account_id to that account (L3429-3433). It never redraws the tree, and a test checks that it does not (L40228).
4. M goes through mark_these_read and then write_flags_or_put_the_row_back. That reaches the_folder_counts_moved (L23775), which sends only FolderCountsMoved. The M path calls no read_the_tree_back.
5. say_the_folder_counts_again (L21438) reads with active_account_id. folder_tree_updates gets labels from get_tags_for_account(account_id), and tags.rs:107 filters by `WHERE account_id = ?1`. folder_tree::rows then adds a Labels heading and one WhichRow::Label(id) row per label (folder_tree.rs L681-691).
6. rows_that_read_differently (folder_tree.rs L959) needs the same length and the same identity at every position, so it returns None. The function logs "counts wait for the next rebuild" and returns. Nothing rewrites the count.

Example: two accounts, A with a label "Receipts" and B with none. The tree was drawn last for B, the person is in A's Inbox and presses M. The tree still says "Inbox, 5 unread" until the next check redraws it.

It is wider than the example. Two accounts that both have labels still fail, because a Label row's identity is the tag id, so even the same name gives different rows. Only two accounts that both have no labels escape.

The changelog's "Known limits" (L1591-1594) does not mention this. The doc comment's "rows came, went or moved" fallback was meant for a tree that changed, not for a tree read for the wrong account. The test reads both times with "acct-1".

The fix is to keep the account id the tree was last drawn for and read with that, or to match rows by identity.

STANDS: I could not refute this. The bug is real at 0b781473.

1. The folder tree shows every account, but its Labels rows come from one account. `folder_tree_updates` reads `get_tags_for_account(account_id)` at L14743, and `folder_tree::rows` adds the Labels heading and one row per label id at L681-691.
2. Each pass of `spawn_mail_sync` (L31962) redraws the tree with its own account's labels via `folder_tree_updates(&cache, &account.id)` at L32313. F9 and start-up hand it every enabled account (doc at L31894).
3. The `FoldersLoaded` arm (L23876-23891) redraws the tree and sets `tree_rows` every time. Nothing filters it by account.
4. Arrowing into another account's folder sets `active_account_id` and does not redraw the tree (L3412-3433, "The tree is not read back").
5. `say_the_folder_counts_again` (L21443) reads the tree again for `active_account_id`. `rows_that_read_differently` (folder_tree.rs L959-964) needs the same identity at every position, so a different set of label ids gives `None`. The function then logs and returns, and the count is not updated.

Labels are made by the person, and a label belongs to one account. So the case needs two or more accounts, at least one label, and a tree last drawn for an account other than the active one. Example: person in A's Inbox, last F9 pass was B, press M, and "Inbox, 5 unread" stays at 5. The M flag change does not wake the inbox watch: `event_for` in imap.rs reports only EXISTS and EXPUNGE. So nothing redraws the tree until the next check.

Nothing at the head commit covers this:
- The doc comment only accepts rows that came, went or moved since the tree was drawn. Here no row changed; the second reading used the wrong account.
- The 13.2-31.2 changelog limits name only a change made during a check of that folder.
- Ledgers 836 and 899 say nothing about multiple accounts or labels.
- The 13.2-31.2 plan and summary do not raise it.
- tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs has three accounts and no labels.

A warning on the first fix the reviewer proposes: it must not set `held.tree_rows = fresh` when the screen differs. Rows are matched to tree items by position, so that would break the position lookups in `the_row_on_screen` and `which_row`. The smaller safe fix is to keep the account id the tree was last drawn with, and read with that id.

STANDS: I could not refute it. At 0b781473, folder_tree_updates (wx_app.rs L14743) adds Labels rows only for the account it is given. Every other kind of row covers all accounts: the folders (L14633-14651), pins and saved searches. So the account the tree was read for changes only the Labels group.

Label ids carry their account. labels_for (L13712) writes them as "{account_id}:{keyword}", and the label manager makes new ids with id_or_new. That means two accounts never share a Label row. If either account has labels, the tree drawn for one account and a fresh reading for the other differ in identity. rows_that_read_differently (folder_tree.rs L959-973) then returns None, and say_the_folder_counts_again (L21461) stops with only a line in the log.

The case is the default state for a two-account user:
- At start, active_account_id is the first account (L1088).
- The check at start, F9 and the schedule all go through every_enabled_account in list order. spawn_mail_sync redraws the tree once for each account (L32313), so the last account's labels stay on screen.
- Both accounts get the same last_checked instant (L31919-31924), so they fall due together and the last account is redrawn last again.
- Arriving at another account's folder only sets active_account_id. Nothing rebuilds the tree (L3412-3433 says "The tree is not read back").
- labels_for creates the starting five the first time any label, rule count, Quick Step or set action runs, so an account that has ever used labels has some.

Result: after M or Delete in the first account, "Inbox, 5 unread" stays stale until the next check. The 13.2-31.2 feature does nothing there.

The only test, tests/the_folder_tree_counts_follow_a_change_made_here.rs (L421-434), reads "acct-1" both times and has no labels, so it cannot catch this.

On severity: this is a bug at the expected load of a few accounts. What goes wrong is a count that stays stale until the next check, which is how it behaved before 13.2. That is not data loss. "Must" fits this review's rule that a bug is "must", though it sits at the mild end.

The proposed fix works and is small. It touches only rows_that_read_differently and say_the_folder_counts_again. Pair each held row with its item on screen by position, look up the fresh label by identity, and reword the rows that differ. Two details: compare the item count with held rather than fresh, and change held labels in place instead of replacing tree_rows with fresh. The other option, keeping the account the tree was drawn for, is larger because FoldersLoaded does not carry an account id and its senders would all change.

duplicate_reports.title: Folder tree count stops updating with two accounts
duplicate_reports.problem: It reads the tree for the active account. But the tree's Labels group holds the labels of whichever account the tree was last drawn for. Each account's check redraws the tree with that account's id, and moving between accounts does not redraw it. When the two accounts' labels differ, the row lists differ, rows_that_read_differently returns None, and the count is never rewritten.
duplicate_reports.concrete_case: Two accounts: A has a label "Receipts", B has none. F9 or the schedule checks both, and the last pass draws the tree for B, with no Labels rows. The person is in A's Inbox and presses M. The new reading for A has the Labels heading and Receipts, the rows on screen do not, so the log says the counts wait for the next rebuild. "Inbox, 5 unread" stays at 5 until the next check. The same happens after arrowing from B's folders into A's.
duplicate_reports.fix: Match rows by identity, not by the shape of the whole list. Build a map from identity to label from the new rows. Then, for each row on screen (by position) whose identity is in the map with a different label, set that item's text. Rows that are only in one list are skipped. Another option is to keep the account id the tree was last drawn with and read with that.

findings.title: A mark on a message the list has not loaded goes to the open account's server
findings.what_this_is: spawn_server_change chooses which account's server to tell by calling owner_of. owner_of looks the message up in the loaded rows and, when it is not there, falls back to the open account (active_account_id).
findings.problem: In All Inboxes the open account is whatever account was last opened, and a conversation's messages in Sent or other folders are not among the loaded rows. Their change is then sent to the open account's server, using the other account's folder path and message number (UID). 13.2-03.1 adds a new caller of this kind: mark_what_was_read now marks a message it read from the store (L13184-13188) and passes that row to spawn_server_change.
findings.concrete_case: Two Gmail accounts, A and B. The last folder opened was in A; then All Inboxes in conversation view. The person presses M on a conversation from B that holds their reply in [Gmail]/Sent Mail as UID 57. Mark reaches the whole account, so the reply is included, but it is not loaded. A's session is told to set the flag on UID 57 in A's Sent Mail, so an unrelated message changes on A, and B's server is never told.
findings.fix: When the row is not among the loaded rows, read its account from the store: cache.get_message(row), then cache.account_of_folder(folder_id), as send_the_marks_on_their_own already does. Refuse when there is none. Never fall back to the open account for a row that came from the store. For mark_what_was_read, the stored MessageItem already carries account_id.
findings.if_we_skip: Read, star and label changes land on another account's mailbox. With the whole-conversation delete setting, so do deletes, through the_account_a_row_is_in, which uses the same fallback.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/presentation/wx_app.rs. L29503-29511: owner_of(&s.messages, &s.accounts, message_row_id, s.active_account_id). L23052-23069: owner_of finds the row in messages, else uses the open account. git show 0b781473:src/application/destinations.rs L537-544: whose_folders_a_move_is_about falls back to the open account. L3322-3331: All Inboxes does not set active_account_id. L12704-12709: toggle_read_state uses TheWholeAccount reach. git show 0b781473:src/data/message_cache/messages.rs L2800-2830: messages_in_conversation with TheWholeAccount covers every folder. L13184-13202: the new store path calls spawn_server_change. L29702: the_session_at(&account) uses that account. .planning/WINDOWS.md ledger 179 records this owner_of fallback as a fault that 'has now happened four times', but not this case.
checker_notes:
STANDS: The finding holds: I walked the path at 0b781473 and the wrong account really gets the change.

1. Startup sets active_account_id to the first account (L1088). Landing on All Inboxes (L3322-3331) does not change it, and selecting a row does not either. The only other writes are at L3311, L3382, L3432 and in the account-list refresh.
2. All Inboxes loads s.messages from cache.unified_inbox, which holds inbox rows only (L8329). Its conversation rows come from conversations_in_every_inbox, and each row records the account it was read in.
3. The M key (L4220) calls toggle_read_state. That calls chosen_messages with TheWholeAccount (L12708). In conversation view, chosen_messages reads the members from the store with messages_in_conversation(thread, read_in.account_id, read_in.folder_id, reach). The ONE_FOLDER reach is `account_id = ?1 AND (?3 = 1 OR id = ?2)`, so B's Sent Mail copy is included (only an All Mail duplicate is dropped).
4. mark_these_read writes each member locally, then calls spawn_server_change with that member's row id, its UID and the_folder_it_is_in, which gives "[Gmail]/Sent Mail". Nothing checks the account on the way.
5. spawn_server_change (L29503-29511) calls owner_of(&s.messages, ...). The Sent row is not in s.messages, so the_message_is_in is None. whose_folders_a_move_is_about(None, Some(A)) then answers A (destinations.rs L537-544), and owner_of resolves that to account A.
6. The worker checks only that an account exists and that the folder path is known (L29550-29568). It then calls the_session_at(&A).set_flag("[Gmail]/Sent Mail", 57, SEEN, read) (L29701-29716). Nothing checks that the folder belongs to the account.

What goes wrong:
- B's server is never told.
- A's unrelated Sent Mail UID 57 gets the flag. Mark unread on an all-read conversation clears \Seen on it, and star does the same kind of damage.
- If A cannot be reached, the change is queued under account_id A with B's folder path.

The ledger does not record this case. Ledger 179 is a different window: a sync during the move dialog. Ledger 563 states the intent that "a command on one of them [reaches] that account", which this path breaks.

Two corrections to the finding, neither of which undoes it:
- The M-on-a-conversation path in All Inboxes is older than 13.2. At 2a4679a9, toggle_read_state already used TheWholeAccount and owner_of already had the same fallback. Phase 13.2 adds another way in: the store-read branch of mark_what_was_read (L13184-13202, commit 127a6f52).
- The suggested fix says send_the_marks_on_their_own already gets the account right. It uses account_of_folder only to name labels, and it still sends through spawn_server_change, so it falls back the same way.

The smallest fix still works: in spawn_server_change, when the row is not loaded, take the account from the store with get_message and then account_of_folder, and refuse if there is none.

STANDS: I could not refute it. The bug is real at 0b781473 and nothing at the head commit covers it.

How it happens:
1. In All Inboxes the loaded rows are only every account's inbox (load_every_inbox, through unified_inbox). The All Inboxes arm at L3322-3331 never sets active_account_id, so it keeps the last account opened, or the first account from startup (L1088).
2. M on a conversation row calls toggle_read_state, which reads the conversation with AConversationReaches::TheWholeAccount (L12704-12709). messages_in_conversation then returns that account's messages in every folder, Sent included (the_scope_over reaches every folder of the account and leaves out only the all-mail duplicates).
3. mark_these_read calls spawn_server_change for every chosen message (L12802-12811), whether or not its state changed.
4. spawn_server_change picks the account with owner_of (L29503-29511). owner_of looks only in s.messages. When the row is not there, whose_folders_a_move_is_about (destinations.rs L537-544) falls back to the open account.
5. The worker then calls the_session_at(&account) on account A, with B's folder path (from the_folder_it_is_in) and B's UID. Nothing checks that the folder belongs to that account.

Result: a message in A with the same path and UID gets marked, or A refuses and B's row is put back with an error. Either way B's server is never told. Star works the same way (star_these). The new 13.2-03.1 path in mark_what_was_read (L13184-13202) reaches the same fallback. That happens after Enter opens a row's own message from the store (open_message_window sets reading_began at L16186) and what_reading_may_mark accepts an unloaded message equal to stands_for.

Checked as already handled, and it is not:
- No shortcut: or ponytail: comment covers it.
- The doc comment on whose_folders_a_move_is_about only excuses rows that record no account, which it calls the ordinary case outside All Inboxes. It does not cover rows missing from the loaded list.
- Ledger 179 is only about the move dialog racing a sync between two owner_of calls.
- Ledger 691 is block_the_sender. Ledgers 563, 755, 756 and 835 are listening checks or unrelated All Inboxes refreshes.
- No 13.2 plan mentions owner_of except one mention of active_account_id in 13.2-31.2.
- The owner_of unit tests (L38381-38424) cover only loaded rows. tests/wired.rs only checks that spawn_server_change contains "owner_of(".

The proposed fix does not break that wired.rs check, as long as owner_of( stays in the body: look up the account from the store for a row that is not loaded, and refuse when none is found. Outside All Inboxes the store's account equals the open account, so nothing changes there.

One correction to the finding: send_the_marks_on_their_own uses account_of_folder only to name labels. It still sends through spawn_server_change and owner_of, so it is not an example of the fix already being applied. The M path existed before 13.2. 13.2-03.1 added a second route to the same fallback.

STANDS: I could not refute it. The finding holds at 0b781473.

What I checked:
- `owner_of` (L23052) looks the row up in `s.messages`. When the row is not there, `whose_folders_a_move_is_about` (destinations.rs L537) falls back to the open account.
- In All Inboxes, `s.messages` holds only the inbox rows that `unified_inbox` returns (L8329). `active_account_id` stays on the last account opened (L3322 does not touch it).
- All Inboxes opens in conversation view by default (ledger 563). Mark read, Star and Label always reach the whole account (`reach_for`, choosing_messages.rs L199). So `chosen_messages` adds the conversation's messages from Sent and other folders, read from the store.
- `mark_these_read` and `star_these` then call `spawn_server_change` for each message. It routes through `owner_of`, so it reaches account A. The worker opens A's session (L29702) and runs `set_flag` on B's folder path and UID (L29711). Nothing checks that the folder belongs to A, and nothing checks UIDVALIDITY (the server's number saying whether UIDs in a folder are still the same).
- So with two Gmail accounts, both of which have `[Gmail]/Sent Mail`, this goes wrong. Star or mark-unread on a B conversation that holds your reply changes A's message with that UID, and B's server is never told.

It matters at the expected load. Two or three accounts, All Inboxes, conversation view and a thread you replied to are all ordinary. "Must" is honest: it writes to the wrong account's mailbox. With the whole-conversation delete setting (not the default), Delete goes through `the_account_a_row_is_in` and uses the same fallback, so it can send A's message to A's Trash, or remove it from A's server for good with Shift+Delete.

Scope: the M, Star and Label routing is older than 13.2. Before 13.2, M already reached the whole account and already used this fallback. 13.2 widened it in two places:
- 13.2-03.1 added the store path in `mark_what_was_read` (L13184).
- 13.2-03 added `the_named_message`, which reads a message from the store (L12647).

Correction to the proposed fix: `send_the_marks_on_their_own` does not route by the stored account. It reads the account only to name labels, and still goes through `spawn_server_change` and so `owner_of`. The smallest fix is to look the account up in the store before falling back to the open one, using the existing `cache.the_account_a_message_is_in(row)` (parts_left_behind.rs L70). `the_whole_message_from_its_own_account` already uses it. Do this once, inside `spawn_server_change`'s worker, which already opens a store, and in `the_account_a_row_is_in`, rather than in each caller.

findings.title: Reply or Forward from a conversation quotes nothing when the text is not downloaded
findings.what_this_is: the_body_a_command_quotes gives Reply and Forward the text to quote. For a message named by the conversation window (acting_on), it reads that message's text from the store.
findings.problem: After a check, the store usually holds headers with no text, and nothing on this path fetches the text. The quote is then silently empty, unlike the list, where selecting a row fetches the text.
findings.concrete_case: Message view. Enter on a threaded row opens the conversation. The person arrows to an older reply they never opened and presses Ctrl+L. Compose opens with 'Fwd:' and an empty body, and it can be sent like that. In the message view nothing fetches the other members' text: spawn_conversation_text_fetch runs only for conversation rows.
findings.fix: When get_message_body finds no text for the named message, stop with a sentence, for example "Its text is not on this computer yet. Open it first.", instead of opening compose with an empty quote.
findings.if_we_skip: People send empty forwards and replies without the quote, and a screen reader user may not notice before sending.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/presentation/wx_app.rs. L19723-19730: Some(named) => body_as_written(cache.get_message_body(named)...). L15720-15723: body_as_written(None) is Plain(""). L3624-3634: the list's own comment says headers without text are 'the ordinary case' and fetches with spawn_body_fetch. L3550-3571 and L3643-3647: the conversation text fetch runs only when showing_conversations(). L5549-5560: ID_FORWARD passes this body to ComposeMode::Forward. L19373: start_reply does the same for replies.
checker_notes: STANDS: The finding holds: I followed the path at 0b781473 and the empty forward does happen. In message view, Enter on a threaded row with two or more loaded messages opens the conversation (wx_app.rs L3822-3891). Moving the cursor in that window never fetches text: wx_thread_view.rs only records which row is chosen and contains no fetch or body read. Ctrl+L is in THE_MESSAGE_KEYS and ends the window with Act{ID_FORWARD, message}. open_conversation_again then sets acting_on and calls the main command handler (L29930-29942). The ID_FORWARD branch (L5549) calls msg_info, which calls the_body_a_command_quotes, which calls cache.get_message_body(named). When that message has no stored text, body_as_written(None) returns an empty Plain text (L15720-15723). Nothing on the way stops it: no check for an empty body and no fetch, and open_compose does not fetch either. In wx_compose.rs L1481-1483, format_forward_body puts the "Forwarded message" line above an empty string, so the forward goes out with no content, and nothing is said about it. Reply has the same flaw: start_reply (L19373) gets an empty quote. The finding overstates how often this happens. Since 10-05, start_the_download fetches every message's text after each check. Reading is on by default and the default budget keeps all text, so most messages have text most of the time. Text is still missing in common situations, though. During the first download, every folder's headers arrive before any text, which takes hours at 200,000 messages. With an 'Up to N GB' budget, older messages, the likely older replies in a conversation, are evicted or never fetched. A message whose text fetch failed also has none. Nothing in the 13.2 plans, the ledger or the changelog states this limit. The fix the finding suggests still fits: when the stored text is missing, refuse with a sentence (or fetch the text) instead of opening compose with an empty quote.

STANDS: I could not refute this finding. Nothing at 0b781473 handles it. the_body_a_command_quotes (wx_app.rs L19714-19733) returns body_as_written(None), which is Plain(""), when the named message has no stored text. Its doc comment covers only the case where no store is open. Commit 6bc7eca8 (13.2-03) added it. The 13.2-03 plan and summary, the changelog entries for the conversation-window keys (changelog L2001-2033), WINDOWS.md and the code all say nothing about text that has not been downloaded. There is no shortcut comment and no test for it.

The path is real. In the flat view, Enter on a message whose conversation has 2 or more loaded rows opens the conversation window (L3801-3891). Nothing in that view fetches the other messages' text: spawn_conversation_text_fetch runs only under conversation view (L3643-3647), and wx_thread_view.rs has no fetch. Ctrl+L in that window is ID_FORWARD (wx_thread_view.rs L71). It runs through the main dispatch under ActingOn (L29938), so msg_info calls the_body_a_command_quotes, and open_compose builds the Forward with an empty body (wx_compose.rs L1481-1483).

One correction to the finding: "usually" overstates how often this happens. The default settings (reading on, all text kept) let the download of everything fetch every message's text after each check (L31311 onward). So the gap is only in specific but real situations:
- Pause Downloading is ticked. spawn_body_fetch on a list row ignores the pause; the conversation path fetches nothing.
- The first download of a large mailbox is still running. It goes newest first in chunks of 50, so older replies arrive last.
- A text size limit (1, 5 or 20 GB) is set and old text has been evicted.
- A message's text failed to download.

Concrete case: flat view, Pause Downloading on. Enter on a threaded row, arrow to an older reply never picked in the list, press Ctrl+L. Compose opens with "Fwd:" and the forward header, and the quoted text is missing with nothing said. A reply drops its quote the same way.

The proposed fix only touches the named path. It refuses with a sentence when get_message_body returns None (or no text). The list path and stored-but-empty messages are untouched, so it breaks nothing else.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473, but it happens less often than the finding says, and "must" overstates it.

What holds: the_body_a_command_quotes (wx_app.rs L19715-19733) reads the named message's text with get_message_body. If that text is missing it returns body_as_written(None), which is empty text (L15720-15723). Nothing in the conversation window fetches text. The tree nodes carry only headers (wx_thread_view.rs L139-151, conversation_nodes L16672-16712). In message view the only fetch is the list's focus handler, which fetches the focused row alone (L3586-3647); spawn_conversation_text_fetch runs only in conversation view. So in message view: Enter on a threaded row, arrow to a member whose text is not here, press Ctrl+L. Compose opens with "Fwd:" and an empty forwarded block (format_forward_body, wx_compose.rs L276-288). This path is new in 13.2-03; before it, the command acted on the list row.

What is overstated:
1. "After a check the store usually holds headers with no text" is wrong. It leans on a stale comment at L3625. Since 10-05, start_the_download runs at the end of every check and brings every kept folder's text, newest first (L31122-31130, L31311-31356). The default text setting keeps everything (keeping_message_text.rs L106-111), and reading is allowed by default (allowed.rs). In steady state a conversation member's text is almost always here.
2. The case therefore needs one of these: the first download of a big folder still running (at 200,000 messages and 50 per chunk, older replies lack text for hours); Pause Downloading ticked; a text size limit that cleared older text; a folder the download does not keep; or a message that arrived seconds ago.
3. "Unlike the list" is only partly true. From the list, Ctrl+L before the fetch lands quotes the placeholder "Downloading this message..." (message_preview is set at L24142 from the update sent at L3629-3631). If that fetch fails, the placeholder stays. So this kind of wrong quote already existed before 13.2.
4. Nothing is lost and nothing sends by itself. The empty quote is in the compose window before the person sends. A reply without a quote is still a normal reply; only an empty Forward is truly useless.

Group: "should" (risky new path with no test, narrow trigger), not "must".

Fix: the proposed refusal is small and works. Slightly better in the same few lines: when get_message_body returns None for the named message, call spawn_body_fetch for it and refuse with "Its text is still downloading. Try again in a moment." The person then does not have to open the message first. Also refuse only Forward, or both? Refusing Reply blocks a reply that does not need a quote. Refusing Forward alone is the minimum that removes the useless case.

Note: before making a private subfolder I wrote copies of wx_app.rs, wx_compose.rs and wx_thread_view.rs from 0b781473 to the session scratchpad root. Those names were already there, so any earlier copies of those files were overwritten. The repository was not touched.

findings.title: A download re-read can undo a mark or delete made a moment before
findings.what_this_is: During the first download, the timer reads the open folder again at most every ten seconds (13.2-09). It does this after the update loop of the same tick.
findings.problem: The rows are read in one tick, but the MessagesLoaded or ConversationsLoaded update that carries them is applied in the next tick, 50 ms later. A key handled in between changes rows that this stale read then overwrites. Before 13.2-09 the read ran inside the update loop and was applied in the same tick.
findings.concrete_case: First download running, message view. The person presses Delete just after a tick read the folder. The row leaves, then 50 ms later the stale rows put it back. It stays until the next re-read 10 s later, or until the folder is opened again if that was the last chunk. M behaves the same way: the row goes back to unread.
findings.fix: Move the `due` block above the `a11y.as_one_turn(|| while let Ok(update) = ui_rx.try_recv() ...)` loop. The rows it reads are then applied in the same tick, with no key handled in between.
findings.if_we_skip: This is the owner's 'shows only after the next sync' complaint, in reverse, on a long first download. A row that comes back can be deleted a second time.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/presentation/wx_app.rs. L6584-6606: the drain loop. L6743-6754: due -> reread_folder_if_open after the drain. L18106-18148: load_folder_messages reads the store on the calling thread and try_sends MessagesLoaded. L79: POLL_MS = 50. L25283-25297: the MoreOfTheFolderArrived arm only marks the folder. The diff of 15babf80 shows the reread used to run inside this arm.
checker_notes:
STANDS: This happens at 0b781473. I traced it step by step.

**The path:**
1. In the timer closure, the drain loop at wx_app.rs L6584-6609 runs first. The `due` block at L6743-6754 runs after it.
2. The `due` block calls `reread_folder_if_open` (L23720). That calls `load_folder_messages` (L18105), which reads the store on the UI thread and `try_send`s `MessagesLoaded(items, AChunkOfTheDownloadLanded)` on `ui_tx`. In conversation view it also sends `ConversationsLoaded` (L18279).
3. `ui_tx` is an `async_channel::unbounded` channel (L1052). Its only reader is the `try_recv` loop at L6585, which has already finished for this tick. So the rows wait for the next tick, `POLL_MS` = 50 ms later (L79, L6804).
4. Before 15babf80, the re-read ran inside the `MoreOfTheFolderArrived` arm, which is inside the drain loop. Its update was picked up by the same `while let` loop, so the read and the apply happened in the same tick. I confirmed this in the diff of 15babf80.

**What happens between the two ticks:**
- **Delete:** the menu arm (L5694-5770) runs on the UI thread. `delete_these` leads to `complete_here_then_tell_the_server` (L26837). That writes the store (`what_happens_here` moves the row to Trash) and calls `take_row_out_of_the_list` (L27970), which removes the row from `s.messages`. Nothing re-reads the folder.
- **M:** `toggle_read_state` leads to `mark_these_read` (L12766), which sets `row.read` and writes the store. Nothing re-reads the folder.
- **Next tick:** the `MessagesLoaded` arm (L23987) does `s.messages = messages.clone()` with no filter. The stale rows replace the fresh ones, so the deleted row comes back, or the row goes back to unread. `ConversationsLoaded` (L24076) does the same to `s.conversations`.

**Nothing corrects it soon:**
- When the server accepts a mark, `spawn_server_change` only sends `StatusUpdated`. It sends no row update.
- `the_folder_due` in bringing_everything_down.rs (L124) needs a new chunk mark and 10 seconds to pass. If the stale read came after the last chunk, nothing re-reads until the folder is opened again or new mail arrives.
- The chunk reason is not spoken, so the person hears nothing.

**How likely:** it is more likely than the 50 ms window suggests. On a large folder the re-read blocks the UI thread for hundreds of ms (the code's own comment gives about 0.3 to 1 second at 200,000 rows). Keys pressed during that freeze are queued. Windows handles queued input before `WM_TIMER`, so those keys land exactly between the read and the apply.

**It can get worse:** if the person deletes the returned row again, `where_a_delete_goes_here` now sees the message in Trash. `where_a_deleted_message_goes` then answers `OffTheServer`, and `deleting_asks` asks nothing for a single message in flat view. So a second Delete deletes the message for good, when the person asked for Trash. Because of that I would group this as must, not should.

**The fix:** move the `due` block above the drain loop. The rows it reads are then applied in the same tick, before any key can be handled.

STANDS: Not refuted. Nothing at 0b781473 already handles it. At wx_app.rs L6584-6609 the update loop empties the channel. Then L6743-6754 reads the open folder on the window's own thread and try_sends MessagesLoaded and, in conversation view (the default), ConversationsLoaded into an unbounded channel. ui_rx is emptied only on that timer (L6585), so those rows are applied on the next 50 ms tick. A Windows timer message only fires when no other input is waiting, so a key pressed during the read or in the 50 ms gap runs first. That makes the window at least the read's time plus 50 ms: about 30 ms for the read at the tester's 12,872 messages, and about a second at 200,000 by the comment at L18097-18100, every ten seconds.

Both key paths change memory and the store at once and send nothing through the channel. M runs mark_these_read (L12766), which writes state.messages and the store. Delete runs complete_here_then_tell_the_server, take_row_out_of_the_list and bring_the_conversation_rows_up_to_date (L26865, L27970, L28071). The MessagesLoaded arm (L23987-23997) replaces s.messages wholesale with no check for changes still waiting. The ConversationsLoaded arm does the same for s.conversations and repaints the changed rows. So the deleted row comes back and a marked row goes back to unread, until the next paced read. If that read was the one after the folder's last chunk, the wrong row stays until something else reads the folder.

The returned row is worse than the finding says. what_happens_here (moves_waiting.rs L375-378) has already moved the cache row into the Trash. A second Delete on the returned row therefore gets from = Trash. where_a_deleted_message_goes (destinations.rs L106-107) then answers OffTheServer, a permanent delete. The Delete arm (L5718) asks a question only for conversations, so nobody is asked. The waiting move would also carry the stale INBOX UID (a UID is the server's number for a message in one folder) from the old row, so it could name a different message in the Trash.

Nothing already covers this. Searched: ledger 851 asks only about speech and responsiveness. The changelog entry (around line 1920) says only that the list is brought up to date every ten seconds. There is no shortcut comment, and no test covers the order of the read and the drain. Before 15babf80 the read sat inside the MoreOfTheFolderArrived arm of that same loop, so its rows were applied in the same tick. The finding's history is right.

The proposed fix works but breaks a test. test_the_timer_reads_the_marked_folder_again_with_a_chunks_reason in tests/everything_comes_down_without_being_asked.rs (L890-933) reads the source between "HOW_OFTEN_TO_LET_HELD_MAIL_GO {" and "let somewhere_to_type = [". Moving the block above the loop reddens it, and its guard records would need re-measuring. A smaller fix keeps the block where it is: empty the channel a second time right after reread_folder_if_open, for example by turning the loop into a closure and calling it twice. One small race remains either way: an update that writes the store earlier in the same pass can still be overwritten by the read. That was also true before 13.2-09. Graded must, not should: the list is wrong at the expected load, and it can lead to a permanent delete.

STANDS: The finding holds at 0b781473. I could not refute it.

How it happens:
1. The update channel (`async_channel::unbounded`) is emptied in one place only, the `while let Ok(update) = ui_rx.try_recv()` loop at L6585.
2. The paced re-read at L6743-6754 runs after that loop. `load_folder_messages` (L18105) reads the store on the UI thread and only queues `MessagesLoaded`. The handler at L23987 then replaces `s.messages` whole on the next tick.
3. Before 15babf80, which is in the range, the re-read ran inside the `MoreOfTheFolderArrived` arm, during the loop. The rows were applied in the same tick. So this is a regression from 13.2-09.

Why a key lands in the gap:
- Delete takes the row out with `take_row_out_of_the_list` (L27970). M sets `row.read` (L12783). Neither one reads the folder again. When the server accepts the flag change, nothing reads it again either. So the stale rows win until the next paced re-read, about 10 s later. After the last chunk they stay until something else reads the folder.

Why it matters at the expected load:
- The read itself blocks the UI thread. The code's own comment puts a 200,000-row read at about 0.3 to 1 s. Conversation view, the default, does a second read on top.
- Keys pressed during that block are queued, and Windows handles input before the next WM_TIMER. So the window is not 50 ms but the read time plus 50 ms, once every 10 s. On a big first download, a few percent of M or Delete presses get undone on screen.

On the group:
- It is a real wrong result, a regression in the class the owner reported, and it is worst at the stated load. The rubric puts a bug in "must".
- There is also a worse follow-on. Press Delete again on a row that came back, and `chosen_messages` uses the stale row's inbox UID (unique identifier, the server's number for a message in one folder). Meanwhile `where_a_delete_goes_here` reads the folder from the store, which is now Trash. So `where_a_deleted_message_goes` answers OffTheServer: a permanent delete, not a move to Trash. I did not follow the server replay to the end.

On the fix:
- Moving the `due` block above the drain loop works. The rows are then read and applied in one handler call, with no key handled in between. MoreOfTheFolderArrived marks taken during that drain are picked up 50 ms later, which is harmless.
- One cost: `what_is_wrong_with_the_timers_reread` in tests/everything_comes_down_without_being_asked.rs looks for the block between "HOW_OFTEN_TO_LET_HELD_MAIL_GO {" and "let somewhere_to_type = [". That test goes red, and must be updated in the same change. So must the guard record in guards/guards.toml anchored on `.the_folder_due(std::time::Instant::now());`.

findings.title: Removing an account and adding it back fails
findings.lines: L152-166 (replace_accounts), L23 and L109-133 (the address check)
findings.what_this_is: replace_accounts writes the Account Manager's list when the person presses OK. It saves every account first, then removes the ones the person took out.
findings.problem: Since 13.2-06, saving refuses an address that another row in the accounts table uses. The removed account is still in the table when the save runs, so the new account is refused, the loop stops, and the removal never happens.
findings.concrete_case: The person removes "Work" (ada@example.com) and adds a new account with ada@example.com, for example to switch from POP to IMAP. The dialog allows it, because its own check only looks at the list without Work. On OK, save_account refuses with "Work already uses ada@example.com. Edit that account rather than adding the address again." Work is never deleted and the new account is never stored. The window still keeps the new account in memory and starts its calendar and contacts syncs. After a restart, Work is back and the new account is gone. The same happens when an edited account takes the address of an account removed in the same sitting.
findings.fix: In replace_accounts, first delete any removed account whose address an account in the new list uses. Then save, then do the other removals as now. Add a test for remove-then-add with the same address.
findings.if_we_skip: Nobody can re-create an account on the same address, and they are told to edit an account they already removed. Before 13.2 this worked, because the old INSERT OR REPLACE wrote over the old row.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/data/message_cache/accounts.rs: L152-166 builds `gone`, runs `self.save_account(account)?` for every account, and only then `self.delete_account(id)?`. L23 `self.refuse_an_address_another_account_uses(account)?`. L109-133 reads `SELECT id, name, email FROM accounts`, which still holds the removed row. src/application/one_address_one_account.rs: who_already_uses refuses when no row with the same address has the candidate's id. src/presentation/wx_account_manager.rs:869 `state.working.remove(idx)` and :1812 `refusal_for(working, typed)` check only the dialog's list. mod.rs: `email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`. wx_app.rs:23237 `cache.replace_accounts(&new)`, then `s.accounts = new` and `bring_what_a_new_account_holds` for each added account, even when the save failed. No test covers remove-then-add.
checker_notes: STANDS: The failure happens as the finding describes, at 0b781473. In the Account Manager, Delete (delete_selected, wx_account_manager.rs:869) takes Work out of the dialog's own list only. Add then gives the new account a fresh uuid (line 1892) and checks its address with refusal_for against that list, which no longer holds Work, so the dialog accepts it. On OK, handle_account_mgr calls cache.replace_accounts(&new) (wx_app.rs:23237). replace_accounts (accounts.rs:152-166) saves every account before it deletes anything, so Work's row is still in the table. When save_account reaches the new account, refuse_an_address_another_account_uses runs SELECT id, name, email FROM accounts and gets Work's row back. who_already_uses then finds the same address under a different id and returns AddressTaken, and the error ends the loop. The delete loop never runs, so Work stays stored and the new account is never written. The refusal comes before credentials::store, so the new account's password is not kept either. The caller announces the error, then still sets s.accounts = new and starts bring_what_a_new_account_holds for the added account. The window keeps working with an account the database does not hold. On the next start, Work is back and the new account is gone. At 2a4679a9 the same save-then-delete order worked, because INSERT OR REPLACE dropped the clashing Work row (email is UNIQUE). The regression arrived with 13.2's ON CONFLICT(id) upsert plus the new address check. The replace_accounts tests cover rename plus add, order, refusing a real duplicate, and the empty list. None covers removing an account and adding one on the same address in the same sitting. The suggested fix (first delete each removed account whose address the new list reuses, then save, then do the other removals) is small and correct.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473, and nothing already handles it.

In the Account Manager, removing an account takes it out of the dialog's working list (wx_account_manager.rs:869). Add checks the new address only against that list (`refusal_for(&working, typed)` at :535, :1812), so the dialog accepts a new account on the removed account's address. The new account gets a fresh uuid (:1892).

On OK, wx_app.rs:23237 calls `replace_accounts(&new)`. That function (accounts.rs:152-166) works out `gone` and then runs `save_account` on every account before any `delete_account`. `save_account` first calls `refuse_an_address_another_account_uses` (L23, L109-133). That reads `SELECT id, name, email FROM accounts`, and the removed row is still there. `who_already_uses` then refuses, because the only row on that address has a different id. The `?` stops the loop, so later saves and every removal are skipped. The caller announces "The accounts could not all be saved. Work already uses ada@example.com. Edit that account...", which names an account the person just removed. It still sets `s.accounts = new` and starts `bring_what_a_new_account_holds` for the account that was never stored. After a restart, Work is back and the new account is gone.

This is a regression from 13.2-06 (044605ba). Before it, `INSERT OR REPLACE` cleared the clashing UNIQUE email row and the later `delete_account` cleaned up.

Nothing covers it:
- No test in accounts.rs tries remove-then-add. `test_a_second_account_on_a_taken_address_is_refused_and_deletes_nothing` keeps the first account in the list.
- No ledger row in .planning/WINDOWS.md mentions it. Rows 846 and 847 are about other cases.
- The changelog entries for MAIL-04 (13.2-06 and 2026-10-19) state no such limit.
- No shortcut comment names it.

Skipping the check for removed ids alone would not work. The case-sensitive `email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` would then fail the INSERT, because `ON CONFLICT(id)` handles only the id, so the removal really must come first.

One change to the proposed fix: do not end those early removals with a bare `?`. If one is refused, it would throw away the other edits, which the doc comment and `test_one_account_that_will_not_go_does_not_throw_away_the_other_edits` exist to prevent. Instead, run them first, collect any error, and carry on with the saves.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473. The Account Manager writes its list once per visit: handle_account_mgr calls cache.replace_accounts(&new) a single time after the dialog closes. delete_selected only takes the account out of the dialog's in-memory list (working.remove), and the add check refusal_for only looks at that list, so Remove "Work" followed by Add on the same address is allowed. Add gives the new account a fresh id (Uuid::new_v4). In replace_accounts, every account is saved before any removal. save_account calls refuse_an_address_another_account_uses, which reads SELECT id, name, email FROM accounts, and the removed Work row is still there. who_already_uses finds a row with that address whose id differs from the new one and refuses the save. The `?` then stops the loop, so delete_account(Work) never runs. wx_app announces "The accounts could not all be saved. Work already uses ada@example.com. Edit that account...", which points the person at an account they just removed. It then sets s.accounts = new anyway and starts the new account's syncs. After a restart, Work is back and the new account is gone. If the new account signs in through the browser (OAuth), run_oauth_flow has already stored its tokens under the new id, so they are left in the credential store with no row that names them. That is the orphaned-secret problem finding #3 set out to stop. Before 13.2, INSERT OR REPLACE against the UNIQUE email column overwrote the old row, so this case worked: this is a regression. It matters at the expected load because removing a broken account and adding it again is a common way to fix a setup, even with only a few accounts. The person is told something went wrong, but they lose what they did and get wrong advice, so "must" (a bug) is honest. The proposed fix is the smallest one that works. Only skipping the check for accounts being removed would not do: the INSERT would then hit the UNIQUE email constraint while the old row exists. So the removed account with the reused address has to be deleted before that save, and the other removals can stay last. One test for remove-then-add on the same address is needed.

STANDS: It reproduces at 0b781473. I walked the path. In the Account Manager, delete_selected (wx_account_manager.rs L854-893) takes "Work" out of state.working straight away. Add then runs show_edit with refusal_for(&working, typed), and the new account gets a fresh uuid (L1890-1892). Work is no longer in working, so the dialog's own check passes. For a browser sign-in account, run_oauth_flow builds AuthManager::new(&account.id, ...) and authorize() calls self.store_tokens (oauth.rs L845), which writes the tokens under the new id. On close, wx_app.rs L23236-23245 calls cache.replace_accounts(&new). replace_accounts (accounts.rs L152-166) works out `gone` = [Work], then saves every account before deleting any. save_account(new) first calls refuse_an_address_another_account_uses. That reads `SELECT id, name, email FROM accounts`, which still holds Work. who_already_uses finds Work on the same address with a different id and returns AddressTaken. So the call fails with "Work already uses ada@example.com...". The deletes never run, Work stays in the table and the new row is never written. The caller only announces the error and then sets s.accounts = new, so the window looks right until a restart. After a restart Work is back, the new account is gone, and its tokens sit in the credential store (the Windows secret store) under an id no row names.

This is a regression from 13.2-06 (9968c188/044605ba). Before it, save_account used INSERT OR REPLACE. Because the table has `email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` (mod.rs L2545), that statement replaced Work's row, and the later delete_account(Work) cleaned up Work's mail and secrets. No test covers removing an account and adding the same address back. The tests at L532, L611 and L888 do not.

Two parts of the finding are overstated, though the core holds. First, the failure is not silent: the error is announced at High priority. Second, the Edit path can also start browser sign-in (L611), so remove and re-add is not the only way to switch. The proposed fix is also incomplete. Because of the UNIQUE(email) constraint, saving the new row while Work's row still exists fails at SQLite even if the code check is skipped: ON CONFLICT(id) does not cover a clash on email. So the fix must also delete the removed accounts before saving a kept or new account that reuses one of their addresses (or delete before saving in general). Keeping every save before every delete, as the finding suggests, still fails. No observation was logged to the task-observer log, because this is a fan-out subagent with no reserved id block and writing one risked an id collision.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473, and 13.2-06 introduced it. Nothing in the code, tests, changelog or ledger covers it.

How it happens:
- delete_selected (wx_account_manager.rs L854-890) only takes "Work" out of the dialog's own list.
- Add gives the new account a fresh uuid (L1892). refusal_for checks only that list, so the new account passes.
- On OK, handle_account_mgr (wx_app.rs L23236) calls replace_accounts(&new). That saves every account before it deletes the removed ones.
