- save_account first runs refuse_an_address_another_account_uses, which reads the stored table. Work's row is still there under a different id, so who_already_uses returns "Work already uses ada@example.com" and the save fails with `?`.
- Because of that early return, Work is never deleted, and any accounts after the refused one in the loop are not saved either.
- The handler then sets s.accounts = new anyway. After a restart Work is back and the new account is gone.
- For a browser sign-in account, AuthManager::authorize has already stored the tokens under the new id (oauth.rs L845, store_tokens before Ok), so they are left with no account row.

Before 13.2 this worked. The old save was INSERT OR REPLACE (2a4679a9 accounts.rs L22), so the old row on the same address was replaced, and delete_account(Work) then cleared Work's secrets. That makes this a regression.

What is not covered anywhere:
- No test does remove plus re-add. The replace_accounts tests at L531-690 and L887-916 use different addresses, or keep the first account.
- Ledger 846, 847 and 848 and the MAIL-04 changelog entry cover the plain second-account case and older orphans, not this one.

Two corrections to the finding:
1. It is not silent. The handler announces "The accounts could not all be saved. Work already uses ada@example.com..." at High. That sentence is confusing because Work was just removed, but it is spoken.
2. The proposed fix does not work on its own. The table has `email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` (mod.rs L2545), and the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE does nothing for a clash on email. So if the check runs against the list being saved and saves still come before deletes, the insert fails with a UNIQUE constraint error while Work's row is still there. Worse, credentials::store has already run by then, so even a password account would leave a secret with no row.

A fix that works: in replace_accounts, delete a removed account before the saves when its address is reused in the new list (or delete all removed accounts first), and run the address check against the new list. The test 'one account that will not go' still holds, because it only needs a refused removal of an unrelated account not to stop the other saves. Add a test that removes an account and re-adds its address under a new id.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473, but the proposed fix would not work.

Why the bug is real:
- `replace_accounts` (accounts.rs L152-166) saves every account first and only then removes the ones that are gone.
- Each save first calls `refuse_an_address_another_account_uses`, which reads `SELECT id, name, email FROM accounts`. At that moment the removed account is still in that table.
- `who_already_uses` only lets an address through when the ids match. A newly added account gets a new id (`show_edit` makes one with `uuid::Uuid::new_v4()`, wx_account_manager.rs L1892).
- The Account Manager's own check (`refusal_for(&working, typed)`, L535) passes, because `delete_selected` already took Work out of `working`.

So this happens: remove Work (ada@example.com), add an account on ada@example.com, press OK.
- The new account is refused with an error, and nothing after it is saved.
- Every removal in that sitting is skipped, not only Work's, because the error returns before the delete loop.
- wx_app.rs L23236-23245 then sets `s.accounts = new` anyway. So the window works with the new account until a restart. After a restart, Work and every other removed account come back, and the new account is gone.
- If the new account uses browser sign-in, its tokens were already stored under its new id. No account row names them, so nothing will ever remove them.

This is a regression from 13.2-06 (044605ba). Before it, `INSERT OR REPLACE` replaced Work's row through the `email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` constraint (a database rule that no two rows hold the same address), and the re-add worked. Load does not matter here: this is a plain bug in one person's normal use, so "must" is the right group.

Two overstatements in the finding:
- It is not silent. wx_app announces at High priority: "The accounts could not all be saved. Work already uses ada@example.com. Edit that account rather than adding the address again." That is misleading, because Work is no longer in the list, but the person does hear it.
- "The usual way to switch it to browser sign-in" is too strong. The Edit path also runs the browser sign-in (`u.use_oauth && u.oauth_access_token.is_empty()`). Remove-and-re-add is one plausible repair, not the usual one.

Why the proposed fix fails: the schema (mod.rs L2545) declares `email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, and `save_account` uses `ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE`, which only covers a clash on the id. Checking addresses against the list being saved and skipping the table read still leaves Work's row in place during the saves. The new row's INSERT then fails with "UNIQUE constraint failed: accounts.email". Worse, `credentials::store` has already run for the new account by then, which leaves the very orphaned secret finding #3 exists to prevent.

Smallest fix that works: in `replace_accounts`, run the removals first without stopping at a refused one. Keep the first error, save every account, then return that error. That still passes "one account that will not go does not throw away the other edits": the rename is saved and the result is still an error.

Add one test: store "work" on ada@example.com, then call `replace_accounts(&[an account "new" on ada@example.com])`. Only "new" should be stored.

duplicate_reports.title: Removing an account and adding it back fails to save
duplicate_reports.problem: The address check reads the stored table. A removed account is still in that table while the saves run, because the deletes come after. So an account removed in this visit still blocks its own address. The dialog's own check passes, because it looks at the dialog's list, where the old account is already gone.
duplicate_reports.concrete_case: In the Account Manager, remove "Work" (ada@example.com), add a new account with ada@example.com (the usual way to switch it to browser sign-in), and press OK. Browser sign-in has already stored the new account's tokens under its new id. replace_accounts then refuses with "Work already uses ada@example.com". Work stays in the database and the new account is never saved. Its tokens stay in the credential store (Windows' secret store) with no account row pointing to them. The window still sets s.accounts to the new list, so it works until a restart. After a restart, Work is back and the new account is gone.
duplicate_reports.fix: Check addresses against the list being saved, not the stored table. Run who_already_uses once over `accounts` at the top of replace_accounts, then save through an inner save that skips the table read. Keep saves before deletes, which the test 'one account that will not go' needs.

findings.title: Each check puts back the unread count of a mark that is waiting
findings.what_this_is: Since 13.2-31.2, database triggers (rules the database runs on every insert, update or delete) move a folder's unread count at once when a message changes here. Each mail check then writes the server's count (its STATUS reply) over that number.
findings.problem: A mark that could not reach the server waits in waiting_flag_changes. The check keeps the row read, but the server's count still counts that message as unread. So the check puts the old number back.
findings.concrete_case: Default settings: changing mail at the server is off (allowed.rs, NOTHING and FOR_TESTING both have `mail: false`). The Inbox has 5 unread messages. The person presses M on 3 of them, and the tree says "Inbox, 2 unread". The gate refuses the push, so the change waits. The next check, from opening a folder or the timer, reads STATUS as 5 and the tree says "Inbox, 5 unread", while all 3 rows still read as read. It stays wrong after every check until changes are turned on.
findings.fix: In set_folder_counts, take the folder's waiting changes into account in the same statement. Join waiting_flag_changes to messages on message_row_id where messages.folder_id is this folder. Subtract waiting changes to read, add waiting changes to unread, and stop at 0.
findings.if_we_skip: For every default user, the number spoken beside a folder is wrong after every check. That is the gap ledger 836 was meant to close. The changelog's known limits name only a change made during a check, not this.
findings.evidence: src/application/mail_sync.rs: :1779 takes `counts` from the server at the start; :2034-2045 the flag pass keeps a waiting flag over the server's (`the_flags_to_keep`); :2070 `cache.set_folder_counts(folder_id, unread, counts.total as usize)`. folders.rs L137 `UPDATE folders SET unread_count = ?1`. wx_app.rs:29682 keeps the change when the push fails. flag_changes_waiting.rs:134-161 maps Error::Security (the gate's refusal, asserted in mail_controller.rs:1912) to ThisComputerRefusedIt and then KeepItAndWait. allowed.rs:136 and :155 `mail: false`. docs/changelog.md:1590-1593 lists the limits. wx_app.rs:32051 replays waiting changes before sync_folder (:32218), so only refused or offline changes are affected.
checker_notes:
STANDS: The finding holds at 0b781473. I walked the default case step by step.

1. Changes at the server start off. `allowed_for` (allowed.rs:1058) falls back to `Allowed::NOTHING`, where `mail` is false. So `MailController` never calls `session.allow_changes()` (mail_controller.rs:493).
2. Pressing M runs `toggle_read_state`, then `mark_these_read` (wx_app.rs:12766). That writes the row as read in the cache first, through `write_flags_or_put_the_row_back`, and the new trigger lowers `folders.unread_count` (mod.rs:2798). The tree says 2.
3. Then `spawn_server_change` runs `controller.set_flag`. The IMAP `set_flag` calls `may_i` and gets `Error::Security` back (imap.rs:1429). `why_the_push_failed` reads that as `ThisComputerRefusedIt`, which means keep it and wait. So `keep_a_flag_change_waiting` stores the change and the row stays read (wx_app.rs:29665-29697).
4. At the next check, `send_the_flag_changes_that_were_waiting` is refused by the same gate and the changes go on waiting (`what_became_of_it`). Then `sync_folder` takes its counts from the server's STATUS reply at mail_sync.rs:1779. The server never heard of the 3 marks, so it still counts 5 unread.
5. In the flag pass, `the_flags_to_keep` writes the waiting read flag over the server's, so the rows stay read and no trigger fires. Then mail_sync.rs:2070 calls `set_folder_counts(folder_id, 5, total)`, and folders.rs:137 writes `unread_count = 5` as it is.
6. `folder_tree_updates` (wx_app.rs:32313) runs for every check, including a check of one folder. It reads `folder.unread_count` straight into `FolderInTheTree::unread` (wx_app.rs:14686). Nothing subtracts the waiting changes.

Result: the tree says "Inbox, 5 unread" while the 3 rows show as read, and every later check writes 5 again until changes are turned on. Nothing in the code, the changelog or the ledger covers this. The 13.2-31.2 plan's premise 5 and the changelog's known limits mention only a mark made during a check. Ledger 836 and 899 do not mention waiting changes. It also goes against the project's own rule D5, where a waiting change wins over what the server says, which the flag pass already follows.

Before 13.2 the tree always showed the server's number, so the number after a check is not new. What is new is that 13.2 now promises the count follows a mark at once: it drops to 2 and then jumps back to 5 for every default user. That is a wrong number spoken by the feature this phase shipped.

The proposed fix is the smallest one: in `set_folder_counts`, subtract waiting read changes and add waiting unread changes for that folder, stopping at 0.

STANDS: I could not refute this finding. Nothing at 0b781473 covers the case.

1. **The mark is kept, not undone.** With mail changes off, which is the default (`Allowed::NOTHING` and `FOR_TESTING` both have `mail: false`), M and the read-on-open path both call `spawn_server_change` (wx_app.rs:12803, 13201). `imap::set_flag` checks the gate first through `may_i`. `why_the_push_failed` reads the gate's `Error::Security` as `ThisComputerRefusedIt`, and that leads to `KeepItAndWait`. So the row stays read and a row goes into waiting_flag_changes (wx_app.rs:29673).

2. **The check puts the old number back.** At the next check, `send_the_flag_changes_that_were_waiting` is refused again, so the change goes on waiting (wx_app.rs:32051). The flag pass keeps the waiting flag through `the_flags_to_keep`, so the row is not touched and no trigger runs. Then mail_sync.rs:2070 calls `set_folder_counts` with the STATUS unread count read at :1779, and folders.rs:137 writes it straight over the count. So the tree goes from 2 back to 5 while all 3 rows still read as read. This repeats at every check until changes are turned on, and every message read while changes are off adds to it.

3. **Nobody has covered it.**
   - **Ledger:** entry 836 and entry 899 in .planning/WINDOWS.md describe only the server's count winning. No ledger entry mentions waiting changes.
   - **Changelog:** its known limits name only a change made while a check is running.
   - **Plan:** 13.2-31.2's premise 5 covers only that same in-check window, and its stated design is "the next check replaces it". That assumes the server already knows about the change, and a waiting change is exactly the case where it does not. The flag pass already handles this case for flags (D5). The count does not.
   - **Tests:** the folders.rs test `test_the_next_checks_count_replaces_the_one_kept_here` has no waiting row, and no test covers a count with a waiting change.

4. **The proposed fix would not break that test.** The test has no waiting rows, and the table has what the fix needs (message_row_id, which_flag, changed_to). Two cautions:
   - Count only rows where which_flag = 'read'.
   - If the same message was also marked on another device, the server's count already includes the change, and subtracting it again makes the count one too low. Stopping at 0 limits this, but it is a known gap the fix should name.

This was not right before 13.2 either: back then the count never moved at all while changes were off. But 13.2-31.2 claims to close ledger 836, and for default users the count now jumps from 2 back to 5 at every check.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473. allowed.rs:136 and :155 set `mail: false` for both NOTHING (the Default) and FOR_TESTING. Under that setting, M changes the row here, and the push then fails with Error::Security from outward::permitted. why_the_push_failed reads that as ThisComputerRefusedIt, so the change is kept (KeepItAndWait), and wx_app.rs:29682 stores it with keep_a_flag_change_waiting. The trigger lowers folders.unread_count at once. At the next check, mail_sync.rs:2033-2044 writes the kept flags. The row was already read, so the trigger's WHEN clause does nothing. Then :2070 runs set_folder_counts with the STATUS unread count, which still counts the message. After a check the tree is rebuilt from cache.unread_count (wx_app.rs:14686), so a person with default settings hears "Inbox, 5 unread" while 3 of those 5 rows read as read. This repeats after every check. No test covers waiting changes in folders.rs, and the changelog limits at docs/changelog.md:1590 name only a change made during a check, so this gap is not ledgered.

On severity: the count after a check is the same number it was before 13.2. What is new is that it drops at the key press and jumps back at the next check, with no new mail. That is a wrong number spoken to a screen-reader user under the default setting. It is not data loss, but the task's grouping puts any wrong-result bug in "must", so "must" is honest. It costs nothing at scale: the table holds one row per message and flag.

The proposed fix has a hole. "Add waiting changes to unread" counts too many after M is pressed twice. Take M, then M again, with mail changes off: INSERT OR REPLACE leaves one waiting change, to unread. The server never heard either change and still counts that message unread. So the fix would turn the server's 5 into 6. A smaller safe fix touches only waiting changes to read. In set_folder_counts, subtract the count of waiting_flag_changes rows with which_flag = 'read' and changed_to = 1 whose message row is in this folder and has read = 1 and deleted = 0, and stop at 0. Leave waiting changes to unread alone. The server's state for those cannot be known here.

One edge remains: a message already read at the server (read on a phone) and marked read here while the change waits would be subtracted once too often. That case is rare. A failing test should be written first: a folder at 5, one waiting read change, then set_folder_counts(5), and expect 4.

findings.title: A filed message with no Message-ID can take another message's number
findings.what_this_is: settle_a_moved_row asks the destination folder which number holds the moved message's Message-ID. If the folder answers with exactly one number, the row on this computer becomes that number. Since 13.2-08, every move a rule makes calls it as well (mail_sync.rs L1390-1415).
findings.problem: A message with no Message-ID header is stored with message_id "". UID SEARCH HEADER MESSAGE-ID "" matches every message that has a Message-ID header (RFC 3501, 6.4.4, zero-length string). So a single answer can be a different message, and nothing reads that message to check. This is the same substring-search shape as ledger 902, in a different function.
findings.concrete_case: The folder Receipts was empty at the last check. Since then a phone filed one receipt into it (UID 7), not yet read here. A rule files an arriving message that has no Message-ID into Receipts. The search for "" answers [7], and the_server_holds_it_at makes the filed row UID 7. When Receipts is read, 7 counts as held, so the receipt never shows, and the filed message comes down a second time under its real number. Deleting the row that shows the filed message's subject sends the delete to 7, which is the receipt.
findings.fix: Skip the search when message.message_id is blank and let the next read bring the message. The fuller fix: read the one number found with server.the_identifier_at and keep it only if renumbered::the_number_confirmed agrees, since that check already refuses a blank identifier. where_it_is_now (L948-969) needs the same blank guard.
findings.if_we_skip: Rarely, but automatically, because rules run with nobody at the keyboard: a row gets tied to the wrong message, and a later Delete of it removes a message the person never saw.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/application/moves_waiting.rs L1031-1042: match server.where_it_is(destination, &message.message_id).await?.as_slice() { [uid] => cache.the_server_holds_it_at(message_row, folder.id, *uid) ... }. mail_sync.rs:659 and filing.rs:53 store message_id with .unwrap_or_default(). imap.rs:1522-1527 sends HEADER MESSAGE-ID {quoted} with no blank check. data/message_cache/moves_waiting.rs the_server_holds_it_at: takes over the number unless another row already sits there. New caller added in fb694c7b: mail_sync.rs L1398 `if let Err(why) = settle_a_moved_row(controller, cache, moving.message_row, &account_id, &into.path)`. Ledger 854/902 cover draft_copy only.
checker_notes:
STANDS: The bug happens at 0b781473, and nothing on the path stops it.

1. A message with no Message-ID header arrives. mail_sync.rs:659 stores it with message_id "" (unwrap_or_default). The IMAP parser gives None for a missing header (imap.rs:1986).
2. apply_rules (mail_sync.rs:1092-1127) does not check the identifier and adds a Moving for it.
3. carry_out_the_moves moves it on the server. After Moved::Moved and cache.move_message, it calls settle_a_moved_row (mail_sync.rs:1398). This caller was added in 13.2-08; in 2a4679a9, mail_sync.rs does not call it.
4. settle_a_moved_row (moves_waiting.rs:1022-1035) reads the row and finds the folder. It has no blank check, and it calls where_it_is(destination, "").
5. That reaches MailController::uids_with_message_id and then ImapSession::uids_with_message_id (imap.rs:1522). may_i passes, since the move already needed write permission. quote_for_search("") returns "", so the server is sent `UID SEARCH HEADER MESSAGE-ID ""`.
6. RFC 3501 6.4.4 says a zero-length string matches every message that has that header. Take a destination holding exactly one message with a Message-ID that is not yet stored here, like the receipt a phone filed. The search answers [7]. The moved message has no header, so it does not match.
7. The match arm `[uid]` calls the_server_holds_it_at(row, folder, 7) (data/message_cache/moves_waiting.rs:503-529). No row sits at (Receipts, 7), so it rewrites the filed row to UID 7 with no further check. Nothing reads what is really at 7, although the trait has the_identifier_at for exactly that.
8. The next read of Receipts compares server UIDs with stored ones (uids_to_fetch at mail_sync.rs:1899). UID 7 counts as held, so the receipt is never fetched. The filed message's real UID is fetched as new and shows a second time. Flag reads for 7 put the receipt's flags on the wrong row. A Delete on that row sends UID 7, which is the receipt.

The codebase already knows a blank identifier must not be searched. mail_across_accounts.rs:342/391 refuses it, and so does renumbered.rs:289. It is not ledgered in WINDOWS.md and not mentioned in the changelog. The harm needs exactly one message with an identifier in the destination that this computer has not read yet. That is rare, but it fires on its own, from a rule with nobody at the keyboard, and it can end in deleting the wrong message. The smallest fix: skip the search when message_id is blank and let the next read bring the message, or confirm the single UID with the_identifier_at before keeping it.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473, and nothing in the commit already handles it.

Why it happens:
- A message with no Message-ID header is stored with message_id "". You can see this at mail_sync.rs:659 `to_incoming` and filing.rs:53, and the test at mail_sync.rs:7458 checks that the stored value is "".
- Nothing on the rule path filters such messages out. After the move, mail_sync.rs:1398 calls `settle_a_moved_row`, which fb694c7b (13.2-08) added inside this range.
- `settle_a_moved_row` (moves_waiting.rs:1013-1043) sends `server.where_it_is(destination, &message.message_id)` with no blank check.
- That call goes through `MailController::uids_with_message_id` (mail_controller.rs:741) to `ImapSession::uids_with_message_id` (imap.rs:1522-1525). These build `HEADER MESSAGE-ID ""`, and `quote_for_search` (imap.rs:2103) does not check for blank either.
- RFC 3501 section 6.4.4 says an empty search string matches every message that has that header line.
- So if the destination holds exactly one message with a Message-ID, the answer is `[that uid]`. The match arm `[uid] => cache.the_server_holds_it_at(...)` then takes it.

The only safeguard is `the_server_holds_it_at` (data/message_cache/moves_waiting.rs:503-530). It lets the row go only when another row already sits at that folder and number. So the harm needs that one message to be on the server but not yet read here, for example filed there by a phone or a server-side filter since the last read. In that case the row is renamed to the other message's number with filed_here=0. That folder's next read treats the number as held, so the real message there never appears. The filed message comes down a second time under its own number. A later Delete or mark on the renamed row goes to the wrong message.

The same function settles replayed moves of the person's own Move and Delete to Trash (`settle_the_row`, L984-1000). `where_it_is_now` (L956-960) also reads a blank search that finds anything in the destination as "already done".

Already handled? No:
- No `trim().is_empty()` guard exists in moves_waiting.rs. The only one is in renumbered.rs:74, which covers the renumbering decision.
- The trait's own doc (L536-539) says a number from `where_it_is` must be read with `the_identifier_at` before it is trusted. `replay_one` does that through `the_number_to_send_to` (L659-664), but `settle_a_moved_row` never does.
- In .planning/WINDOWS.md, ledgers 854 and 902 cover only draft_copy's removal and replacement.
- The changelog has no limitation entry for this.
- The only test with a blank identifier (moves_waiting.rs:3235-3275) covers the cross-account path, not this function.

The proposed fix is safe:
- A blank guard that calls `let_the_next_read_bring_it` gives the same result as today's `_` arm for an empty or many-number answer.
- The fuller fix goes through `server.the_identifier_at` and `renumbered::the_number_confirmed`. That check already refuses a blank identifier and compares the bare forms, so it also closes the general "one ID contains another" case. Its cost is one header fetch per settled move, plus extra scripted lines in tests that use a real controller transcript. It changes no other behaviour.

The trigger is rare: a message with no Message-ID, and a destination holding exactly one message with one that this computer has not read yet. The result is still a wrong row and a possible delete of a message the person never saw, which is a correctness and data-loss bug.

STANDS: I could not refute it. At 0b781473, settle_a_moved_row (moves_waiting.rs L1013-1043) runs where_it_is(destination, &message.message_id) without checking for a blank identifier. A message that arrives with no Message-ID header is stored with message_id "" (mail_sync.rs:659 uses unwrap_or_default, and imap.rs:1986 passes on the parser's None). The search then goes out as HEADER MESSAGE-ID "" (imap.rs:1522-1527, quote_for_search makes ""). Under RFC 3501, section 6.4.4, a zero-length string matches every message that has a Message-ID header at all.

When the destination holds exactly one other message that has an identifier and that message is not yet held on this computer, the_server_holds_it_at finds no row at that number. So it rewrites the moved row to that number and clears filed_here. From then on the next read treats that number as held: the other message never shows, the filed message comes down a second time under its real number, and a Delete on the wrong row goes to the other message.

The other guards hold only by luck of the folder's contents. A folder holding zero or several identified messages falls back to the next read. A folder whose one identified message is already held also falls back, because another row sits at that number.

This exposure is new in 13.2. Before 13.2 only replayed waiting moves reached this code. Since fb694c7b (13.2-08), every rule move calls it at mail_sync.rs L1398, automatically and with nobody at the keyboard. The ledger does not cover it: 854 and 902 name only the draft path.

The project already treats a blank identifier as something you cannot search for. renumbered::what_it_needs returns PutItBack when the identifier is blank, and the_number_confirmed refuses a blank one. mail_across_accounts.rs L1001-1004 says so in words: "Real mail does" arrive without one. So this function is the one place left out.

Is "must" honest? It is rare, not frequent. It needs a message with no Message-ID, a rule that files it, and a destination holding exactly one identified message that this computer has not read yet. It is not a load problem. But it is a real wrong result that hides a message for good and can send a delete to a message the person never chose, which meets the "bug" bar for must.

The proposed fix is the smallest one that works. One guard at the top of settle_a_moved_row: when message.message_id.trim() is empty, call let_the_next_read_bring_it. That covers both the replay caller and the rule caller, plus one case to hold it. The fuller exact-read fix and the where_it_is_now guard are optional extras. where_it_is_now existed before 13.2.

findings.title: The download of everything takes new mail before the check, so rules never run on it
findings.what_this_is: uids_to_fetch picks which message numbers a sync fetches. 13.2-08 (#12) made it take every message above the newest one held, which is new mail, so that the check's rules see all of it.
findings.problem: sync_folder is shared. The download of everything calls it with filtering None and MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere, which always lists the whole folder (what_to_ask_for L557-559). So each download chunk also takes all new mail, now without the 500 bound, stores it with no rules, and counts nothing as arrived. The download runs alongside checks and takes no account turn. The fix for #12 covers the check and leaves the download path that #12 named.
findings.concrete_case: A first download of a 200,000-message Inbox is running, with a chunk every few seconds. A message from a blocked sender arrives and IDLE wakes a check. The download's next chunk lists the Inbox first and stores the message with no rules. The check then finds it already held: fetched 0, no rule runs, no new-mail announcement, and the blocked sender's mail sits in the Inbox.
findings.fix: In sync_folder, when `wanted` is MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere, fetch only the part below the newest held (drop the `arrived` half of the partition), so new mail is left for the check. That is one match on `wanted` around L1897.
findings.if_we_skip: During a download, which can run for hours, new mail is silent and skips the person's rules, including blocking.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/application/mail_sync.rs L400-418: partition(|uid| newest_held.is_some_and(|newest| *uid > newest)); arrived is taken whole. L557-559: MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere returns EveryUid. L1897: `let wanted = uids_to_fetch(on_server.uids(), &stored, limit);` with no check of `wanted`. wx_app.rs:31513-31530 runs the download chunk as sync_folder(controller, &cache, folder, folder_id, INITIAL_FETCH_LIMIT, None, MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere). wx_app.rs:31391 `stop` reads only downloading.paused. The download never calls one_check_at_a_time; its only caller is wx_app.rs:31971. The test comment at mail_sync.rs ~6800 says the download 'runs no rules and counts nothing as arrived'.
checker_notes:
STANDS: This reproduces at 0b781473. The download's header chunk (wx_app.rs:31518-31532) calls sync_folder with no rules and MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere. what_to_ask_for (mail_sync.rs:562-564) answers EveryUid for that mode, so the chunk lists the whole folder. uids_to_fetch (L406-416) then puts every unheld uid above the newest held into `arrived` and takes all of them. upsert_messages stores them, and apply_rules is skipped because filtering is None (L1916-1919).

Nothing keeps the download and a check apart:
- start_the_download only checks running, paused and the retry wait (L31360).
- The check's one_check_at_a_time turn (L31970) is not taken by the download.
- No other code reads the downloading state to hold a check back.

What the check finds afterwards:
- When it runs, `stored` already holds the new uid. A resumed listing asks only above it, and a full listing filters it out as held.
- So fetched is 0. apply_rules gets no rows, and WhatArrived counts nothing.
- The download's own closing WhatArrived reports folders and text with matches_with_a_sound 0, so no new-mail sentence is said.
- blocking.rs:1-10 confirms a block is just a rule, so the blocked sender's mail stays in the Inbox.

How likely it is:
- With an IDLE wake, it is a race, because the check does several round trips before its listing.
- With scheduled checks it is close to certain, since header chunks run back to back with no wait for as long as the Inbox is partly held. Every new account's first download of a large Inbox goes through this window.

Two notes:
- The bug was already there before 13.2. At 2a4679a9, uids_to_fetch took the newest unheld uids first, so the download picked up new mail too. 13.2-08's plan names this download path as the cause of #12 and fixed only the check's half.
- The proposed fix is safe. If the download leaves new mail for the check, where_a_folder_stands reports StoppedComingDown (bringing_everything_down.rs:195) once a chunk brings nothing. So the download does not spin.

It is a real bug with a concrete case: missed rules, including blocks, and a silent arrival. Under the review's own groups a bug is "must".

STANDS: I couldn't refute it. The race is real at 0b781473, and nothing in the tree covers it: no code, test, `shortcut:` comment, changelog line or WINDOWS.md entry.

What the code does at the head commit:
1. `uids_to_fetch` (mail_sync.rs:400-418) takes every missing uid above the newest one held, with no limit. The download's chunk calls `sync_folder(..., INITIAL_FETCH_LIMIT, None, MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere)` (wx_app.rs:31519-31532). `what_to_ask_for` always lists every uid for that mode (L562), and the chunk passes `filtering` None, so it stores new mail with no rules and counts nothing as arrived.
2. The download and a check run at the same time on the same account. Each check sends `MailboxWatchRequested` and then `DownloadRequested`, so the watch is live while the download runs. A watch waking calls `spawn_mail_sync(..., Some(path), WhateverHasChanged)` (wx_app.rs:25275). The download never takes `one_check_at_a_time`, and its `stop` reads only `downloading.paused`.
3. Both share one session through `the_session_at`, so their commands take turns one by one. The download also starts with the folder on screen, then the Inbox. So while the Inbox is incomplete, the next download chunk can list and store a new message before the check reads `stored`. The check then finds nothing to fetch: no rules run (blocked sender, filing), and `WhatArrived` sends no announcement or sound.
4. Nothing later catches up. `apply_rules` runs only on rows a check or the POP path just stored, plus the filters.rs:1698 call. The cache records nothing like "rules not yet run".

Two points against the finding's framing, neither of which refutes it:
- The race existed before 13.2. At 2a4679a9 the download also took the newest 500 missing uids, and new mail is always among the newest. 13.2-08 only removed the 500 cap on that part.
- It does contradict what 13.2-08 set out to do, which was "every new message reaches the rules once". It also contradicts the changelog line "Every new message reaches your rules". The 13.2-08 plan's premise 1 looked at the download only straight after a check, not new mail arriving while it runs.

The proposed fix as written would break something else. In download mode, if a folder's only gap is new mail above the newest held, a chunk with the `arrived` part removed brings nothing new. `stopped_coming_down` (bringing_everything_down.rs:155) then marks the folder StoppedComingDown, the folder is not asked again this run, and the person hears a false "The mail server stopped sending {folder}". The fix also needs one of these:
- leave out the new mail when the download compares what it holds with the server's total, or
- run the account's rules on the chunk's new mail, and count it, under the account's turn.

STANDS: I could not refute this. The race really happens at 0b781473.

1. Both paths share one function. The download chunk (wx_app.rs:31518-31531) calls sync_folder with no rules and MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere. what_to_ask_for (mail_sync.rs:562-563) then always lists the whole folder. uids_to_fetch (L406-417) takes every uid above the newest held, so the chunk takes any new mail, saves it (L1910) and runs no rules (L1916-1919).

2. Nothing keeps the download and a check apart. stop() reads only downloading.paused (31391), and only the user's menu item sets it (31739). The download never takes one_check_at_a_time; its only caller is the check (31971). Both use the same shared session (the_session_at), so their server commands take turns one at a time.

3. The check usually loses. A check woken by IDLE (the server pushing "new mail" to a waiting connection) first replays moves, sends waiting flags, retries drafts, lists folders, then reads `stored` (L1809). If a download chunk saved the message before that read, the check fetches 0: no rules, no announcement (fetched feeds `arrived`, 32228-32229). The download's own end sentence sends matches_with_a_sound: 0 and says "No rules run over a download of everything" (31652). If the watch is refused (ledger 523 records two refusals on the tester's account), only the scheduled check is left, and a chunk every few seconds wins almost every time.

4. It matters at the expected load. The Inbox comes first in the download, after the folder on screen (place_in_the_order). A first download of 200,000 messages at 500 a chunk takes hours, so for those first hours new mail is silent and skips blocking and filing rules. That is a screen-reader user's first experience of the app. It also makes the 13.2 changelog headline "Every new message reaches your rules" false during that window, and nothing in the ledger records it.

5. On the group: the reviewer filed it as "should" while calling it a bug. By the standard a bug is "must". To be fair, it is older than 13.2: the old uids_to_fetch at 2a4679a9 took the newest 500 missing, which already put new mail first, and the 13.2-08 summary says the download chunk "call[s] it unchanged". So 13.2 did not cause it, but it claimed to fix this outcome and left this path open.

6. The proposed fix is the smallest that works. When `wanted` is MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere, fetch only the uids below the newest held. A folder holding nothing has no newest held, so it still takes its newest 500. Get Older Messages runs through the download, so it is unaffected. Passing rules to the download instead would run them over old back-filled mail, which the code at L1912-1915 deliberately avoids. One small side effect: if new mail is still unfetched when a folder's older mail is done, the next chunk brings nothing, and the folder ends as "stopped coming down" until the next check takes the new mail. That is harmless.

7. It needs a red test: a sync_folder case with MoreOfWhatIsAlreadyThere where the server holds a uid above the newest held, asserting that uid is not fetched.

findings.title: A feed's secret address goes into the log when a fetch fails
findings.what_this_is: When a calendar feed cannot be fetched, this helper turns the network error into the sentence the sync reports. 13.2-14 rewrote it so the sentence names only the host, because a feed address often holds a private token.
findings.problem: Only the timeout branch follows that rule. Every other failure prints reqwest's own error text, and reqwest ends that text with "for url (the whole address)". So the token still reaches the log and the spoken message.
findings.concrete_case: Someone subscribes to Google's secret address https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/ada%40gmail.com/private-9f8e7d/basic.ics. The laptop is offline, so DNS fails. result.errors gets "Calendar feed: Network error: ICS fetch failed: error sending request for url (https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/ada%40gmail.com/private-9f8e7d/basic.ics)". wx_app writes it with tracing::warn! on every background sync while offline. Following a calendar link hands the same text back to be spoken. Anyone who gets the log (testers send logs) can read the whole calendar.
findings.fix: Take the error by value and print it without its address: `Error::Network(format!("{layer}: {}", failed.without_url()))`. Add one case beside the timeout case: a refused connection to an address ending "?token=s3cret" must not say "s3cret".

findings.title: Feeds that start with a byte-order mark stop refreshing
findings.what_this_is: To enforce the 20 MB cap, fetch_ics now reads the feed chunk by chunk and then turns the bytes into text with String::from_utf8_lossy.
findings.problem: Before 13.2 it used reqwest's text(), which decoded with the charset named in Content-Type and removed a byte-order mark (BOM: invisible bytes some Windows tools put at the start of a file). Now the BOM stays, so the first line reads "\u{FEFF}BEGIN:VCALENDAR". parse_ics only accepts a feed when some line starts with BEGIN:VCALENDAR after trim_start, and trim_start does not remove U+FEFF, so the whole feed is refused. A feed sent as windows-1252 also turns é into the replacement character now. The comment "Lossy, as text() decoded it" is wrong.
findings.concrete_case: A school feed written by a .NET tool starts with bytes EF BB BF then "BEGIN:VCALENDAR". It refreshed before this phase. Now every refresh reports "That address did not answer with a calendar. Nothing on this calendar was changed here.", and following a link to it fails the same way.
findings.fix: Decode the collected bytes the way text() did: take the charset from Content-Type and use `encoding_rs::Encoding::for_label(..).unwrap_or(UTF_8).decode(&arrived)`. encoding_rs is already built as a reqwest dependency (Cargo.lock), so the build gains no new code. The smallest partial fix is to strip a leading EF BB BF before from_utf8_lossy. Add a case with a BOM-prefixed feed.
findings.if_we_skip: Some real feeds that worked before this release stop updating, and the error blames the address.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/service/ical_subscription.rs L94-95 `// Lossy, as text() decoded it.` / `Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&arrived).into_owned())`; git show 2a4679a9:src/service/ical_subscription.rs L45-48 used `response.text()`. ical_subscription.rs L149-151 refuses unless `caldav::opens_with_ignoring_case(line.trim_start(), "BEGIN:VCALENDAR")`; caldav.rs L1264 compares bytes from position 0. Cargo.toml L76 reqwest 0.13 with default features; reqwest-0.13.4 Cargo.toml `default = ["default-tls", "charset", ...]`; src/async_impl/response.rs L163-166 text() calls text_with_charset, L208-222 reads the charset and calls encoding.decode; encoding_rs src/lib.rs L3039-3046 decode() strips a BOM. Cargo.lock lists encoding_rs under reqwest 0.13.4.

So text() went through text_with_charset("utf-8") and encoding.decode(). That decode honours the charset named in Content-Type and removes a byte-order mark (BOM, the invisible bytes EF BB BF some Windows tools put at the start of a file). reqwest's own documentation says "the BOM is stripped".

At the head commit, fetch_ics (L76-95) collects the chunks and returns String::from_utf8_lossy(&arrived). That keeps U+FEFF at the start of the text. Nothing on the way strips it. git grep for feff or BOM handling finds only message_files.rs, hidden_text.rs and test strings.

Both callers pass the text straight to parse_ics:
- caldav_sync.rs:1206 calls fetch_and_parse, then parse_ics.
- The followed-link path is wx_app.rs:19557, then read_into_the_calendar, then opening::read_calendar_file, then parse_ics.

parse_ics (L149-151) asks whether any line passes opens_with_ignoring_case(line.trim_start(), "BEGIN:VCALENDAR"). opens_with_ignoring_case (caldav.rs:1264) compares bytes from position 0. Rust's trim_start removes only White_Space characters, and U+FEFF is not one. A normal feed has a single BEGIN:VCALENDAR, on its first line, so with a BOM no line matches. parse_ics returns Error::Protocol("That address did not answer with a calendar...").

What the user sees: in the sync path, that error is pushed as "Calendar feed: ..." and the function returns before anything changes. Events are not lost, but the feed never refreshes again. The followed-link path reports the same failure.

A feed sent as windows-1252 is also now decoded as lossy UTF-8, which turns é into the replacement character. That is a regression too. The comment "Lossy, as text() decoded it" is false.

Nothing marks this as a known limit: there is no shortcut: comment, no changelog note and no WINDOWS.md ledger entry. No test covers a BOM or a charset. The change came in 9fa1b314/2ec8fe0d (13.2-14).

With that feature, text() calls text_with_charset("utf-8"), which picks the encoding from Content-Type and runs `encoding.decode`. That decode strips a byte-order mark (BOM), and reqwest's own docs say so. Commit 2ec8fe0d (13.2-14, audit finding #20) replaced text() with chunked reading plus `String::from_utf8_lossy(&arrived)`, which keeps EF BB BF as U+FEFF and ignores the charset. The comment "Lossy, as `text()` decoded it" is therefore wrong. parse_ics, unchanged in this phase, refuses the whole feed unless some line passes `caldav::opens_with_ignoring_case(line.trim_start(), "BEGIN:VCALENDAR")`. trim_start removes only White_Space characters, and U+FEFF is not one. opens_with_ignoring_case (caldav.rs L1264) compares bytes from position 0. So a feed whose only BEGIN:VCALENDAR line starts with a BOM now fails with "That address did not answer with a calendar. Nothing on this calendar was changed here." Data is not lost, since an error leaves the calendar unchanged. But feeds that refreshed before this phase now refuse, which is a real regression.

6. The comment "Lossy, as text() decoded it" is false.

Feeds with a BOM do exist; parsers in other languages have had bug reports about them. No data is lost, because the refusal leaves the calendar's events untouched. But a feed that refreshed before this phase now fails on every refresh, and the error blames the address. A regression that gives a wrong result is a bug, so "must" fits the rubric.

Fix: the encoding_rs route needs a new line in Cargo.toml and is only needed for the rare feed that declares a charset other than UTF-8. RFC 5545 makes UTF-8 the default. The smallest full fix for the regression is one line in parse_ics: in the BEGIN:VCALENDAR check, also trim a leading '\u{feff}', for example `line.trim_start().trim_start_matches('\u{feff}')`. Add one test with a BOM-prefixed feed. Putting the fix in parse_ics also covers opened .ics files. findings.title: A cut-short CardDAV answer deletes contacts here
findings.what_this_is: cards_in reads the server's answer to "send me every card". Since 13.2-21 the CardDAV sync treats that answer as the whole address book and removes every contact here that the answer does not name.
findings.problem: A response block with no card text in it is skipped without being counted. So an answer the server cut short, or a card sent without its text, still looks complete (could_not_be_read stays 0), and the contacts it left out are removed here.
findings.concrete_case: The CardDAV standard (RFC 6352, section 8.6, truncation of results) lets a server stop after, say, 1,000 cards and add one block with status 507 for the address book itself. That block has no card, so it is skipped and could_not_be_read stays 0. take_off_who_a_whole_answer_left_out then drops the other 500 contacts from this computer, and they may never come back because later answers are cut the same way. A card the server answers with a 404 for its address-data, or a block with no href (named as the empty string), is removed the same way.
findings.fix: In cards_in, count a block that has no card text instead of skipping it quietly: `let Some(card) = the_card_in(block) else { sent.could_not_be_read += 1; continue; };`. The existing `could_not_be_read == 0` guard then skips the removal pass, and the sync already says that some cards could not be read. Add one case: a 507 block plus one card removes nobody.
findings.if_we_skip: On a server that limits its answers, hundreds of contacts disappear from this computer with nobody having deleted them.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/service/carddav.rs L312-319: `let Some(card) = the_card_in(block) else { continue; };`. Only a failed vCard parse adds to could_not_be_read (L316-318). git show 0b781473:src/application/carddav_sync.rs L233-242: `if arrived.could_not_be_read == 0 { let named = arrived.cards.iter().map(|card| card.url.as_str()).collect(); contacts_sync::take_off_who_a_whole_answer_left_out(...) }`. `git grep -n 507 0b781473 -- src/service/carddav.rs` finds nothing. The removal pass came in with b0fc8b53 (13.2-21). No test in carddav.rs covers a block without card data (listed with `git show 0b781473:src/service/carddav.rs | grep -n 'fn test_'`).

1. The live sync is wired up. `wx_app.rs:32580-32587` calls `sync_carddav_address_book` with `AnAddressBookServer`, and its `whats_in` calls `CardDavClient::cards` (carddav.rs:478).
2. `cards` sends `ASKING_FOR_THE_CARDS`, which has no limit, so any cut is the server's own choice.
3. `refused_with` only checks `is_success()`, so the 207 status a cut-short answer must use (RFC 6352) passes and the text goes to `cards_in`.
4. `cards_in` (carddav.rs:312-315) does `let Some(card) = the_card_in(block) else { continue; };`.
   - The extra block has the address book's own href, a 507 status and no `address-data`.
   - So `the_card_in` returns None and the block is skipped without being counted.
   - Only a failed vCard parse adds to `could_not_be_read`, and nothing in carddav.rs, carddav_sync.rs or contacts_sync.rs looks for 507.
5. In `sync_carddav_address_book` (carddav_sync.rs:233), `could_not_be_read == 0` is true, so `take_off_who_a_whole_answer_left_out` runs.

Apple's Calendar and Contacts Server is one server I believe does this, at a default limit of 1,000; I recalled that rather than checked it. A server that answers 404 for one card's address-data hits the same path.

**Result:** at the head commit, the contacts left out of a cut-short answer are removed from this computer, and nothing brings them back while the server keeps cutting at the same limit.

**Severity:** a little overstated, but still "must".
- The contacts are dropped here only. The code says "Dropped rather than deleted", so no deletion goes to the server.
- A contact with an unsent local change, or one waiting on a choice, is kept.
- So this is lost contacts in the app, not on the server. They still vanish with nobody having deleted them, and the sync summary reports them as deleted. That is a wrong result.
- It needs a server that cuts answers short and an address book bigger than its limit. That is uncommon but plausible for one person with a large or work address book.
- The existing `could_not_be_read == 0` guard was written to stop removal after an incomplete answer, and this is a hole in it.

**Fix:** the proposed one-line change, counting a block with no card text as unreadable, is the smallest that works. It reuses the existing guard and the existing error line. One known side effect: a server that also lists a block that is not a card would get a lasting "1 card(s) could not be read" message and no removals. That is the safe direction.

findings.title: A note edited or moved during a notes read is overwritten
findings.what_this_is: take_what_has_arrived reads every note here once. It then fetches each changed note from the backend over the network and writes the backend's copy over the row it read at the start.
findings.problem: The row it writes, and the pending flag it checks before holding a conflict, both come from that first read. An edit, pin or move made while the fetches run is written over. This is the read side of the push race 13.2-20 fixed, and 13.2-20 touched this function without closing it.
findings.concrete_case: The phone changes the note "Shopping". On this computer the person saves an edit to "Shopping" while the sync is fetching notes. The read still sees the old row, pending false, so it skips the conflict hold. write_it_down then saves the phone's words with pending false, and the local edit is gone with no question asked. A note moved in that window (Move saves a new id and deletes the old row) is written back in its old folder, so it now shows twice.
findings.fix: Read the note again by id just after its fetch, and decide on that copy: `let ours = ours.and_then(|n| cache.get_note(&n.id).ok().flatten());`. A waiting edit is then held, and a removed row is not made again. The other way is to guard the write with `WHERE updated_at = ?`, as a_backend_took_the_note now does.
findings.if_we_skip: Rarely, but each time it happens a person's own note edit is lost without a word, which is the outcome 13.2-20 set out to end.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/application/notes_sync.rs: L728 `service.notes_it_holds(container).await`, then L740 `cache.get_all_notes_for_account(account_id)` once. L790 `service.what_a_note_says(container, &one).await` inside the loop. L843-849 holds only when `here.pending` from the snapshot. L850 `write_it_down(cache, folder, ours, &said)`. L890-900 builds the row from `..ours.clone()` with `pending: false`, and L922 calls `cache.save_note(&note)`. data/message_cache/notes.rs L894-910: the editor's Save (the_person_changed_the_note) sets pending = 1 from the window's own connection. notes.rs L487-560: move_a_note_the_backend_holds saves a new id and deletes the old row.
checker_notes:
STANDS: I traced the bug through the code at 0b781473 and it happens as described.

How the sync runs: F5 or Sync Now in Notes calls sync_the_module, which calls spawn_notes_sync (wx_app.rs:32430 and 32782). That runs sync_notes on a worker thread with its own database connection. The editor's Save (wx_app.rs:3048) writes through the window's connection at the same time.

Walking take_what_has_arrived:
1. All of the account's notes are read once (L740) and the read finishes. No lock is held after that.
2. A note whose marker moved is fetched over the network (L790). While that fetch runs, the person's Save calls the_person_changed_the_note (notes.rs:903), which sets new words, pending = 1 and a new updated_at.
3. When the fetch returns, the "same words" check (L813) and the pending check (L843) both use the old copy from step 1. That copy has the old words and pending false, so no conflict is held.
4. write_it_down (L890-900) builds the row from the old copy with the phone's words and pending false. save_note (notes.rs:326) is an upsert: it updates the row if it exists and inserts it if not. So it writes over title, body, pinned, pending and updated_at. The edit is gone and the flag that would send it is cleared. A pin made in that window (toggle_note_pin) is undone the same way.

The move case also holds. move_a_note_the_backend_holds (notes.rs:487-558) saves the note under a new id and deletes the old row. The upsert then inserts the old id again in its old folder, carrying the backend's name. deleted_here was read before the loop (L754), so it does not stop this. No pass in notes_sync removes a local note that the backend no longer lists, so the duplicate stays.

No guard prevents it:
- is_held_for_a_choice (L783) only covers notes already waiting on a choice.
- The marker check (L786) is passed, because the phone moved the marker.
- The test service's `meanwhile` hook runs only in `write` (the push), never in what_a_note_says, so no test covers this.
- I found no entry in the project's list of open items (.planning/WINDOWS.md), and no changelog note, saying this is a known limit.
- 13.2-20 added the updated_at guard to a_backend_took_the_note and a fresh read to keep_what_the_backend_could, but left write_it_down as it was. That is the "fixed in one caller, shared function still broken" pattern.

Two caveats:
- This is older than 13.2. 13.2 did not cause it; it only changed this function's call at L817.
- The first fix offered is not complete for a move. If the note is read again and is now missing, `ours` becomes None, and write_it_down's None branch makes a new copy under a new uuid. The fix must skip the write when the first read had a row and the second read has none. Or use the guarded write: `WHERE updated_at = ?` on the old copy's stamp, and insert only when there was no old copy.

I put it in "must" because it is silent loss of the person's own edit, the same kind of loss audit finding #1 put in "must" and 13.2 set out to end. The time window is narrow, and the person has to start the sync themselves.

STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473, and nothing at that commit covers it. The sync runs on a worker thread with its own database connection (spawn_notes_sync opens a second MessageCache there), so the notes window stays usable while the sync runs. take_what_has_arrived reads every note once, at L740. It then awaits what_a_note_says for each changed note, one network round trip each, so the gap covers the whole loop. Within that gap the editor's Save (the_person_changed_the_note) sets new title and body and pending = 1. Pin (toggle_note_pin) and Move (move_a_note_the_backend_holds) also write in that gap.

What happens with the old copy:
- **Edit:** the stale row has pending false, so the conflict hold at L843 is skipped. write_it_down builds the row from the stale copy with pending false, and save_note's upsert overwrites title, body and pending. The edit is lost after the window said "Note saved".
- **Pin:** the old pin value is written back.
- **Move or delete:** the old row is gone, so the upsert inserts it again. The note shows twice, or a deleted note comes back. This stays, because deleted_here was read before the move or delete, and a backend removal never takes a row away here.

Already handled? No:
- 13.2-20 fixed only the push side (a_backend_took_the_note, keep_what_the_backend_could). In this function it changed only the argument passed at L817. Its plan (premise 3) mentions the read only for a note that was never marked waiting.
- The changelog line of 2026-10-17 talks about a change made "while a sync was sending" it, which is the push side.
- No ledger row in .planning/WINDOWS.md names this.
- No shortcut: or ponytail: comment marks it.
- No test drives it: the test stand-in's what_a_note_says has no `meanwhile` hook, and only leave_a_note_saying has one.

The proposed fix is wrong as written. With `ours.and_then(|n| cache.get_note(&n.id).ok().flatten())`, a moved or deleted row turns into None. write_it_down then takes its None branch and makes a new row (a fresh note- id, the old backend name, the old folder). That is the duplicate the fix says it prevents. The `WHERE updated_at = ?` version has the same hole, because the upsert inserts when the row is missing. Smallest correct fix: after the fetch, read the row again by id. If it was there before and is now gone, `continue`. Otherwise decide the pending/conflict question and do the write on that fresh copy. Better still, do the read and the write in one immediate transaction, as a_backend_took_the_note does. Add a test with a `meanwhile` hook in what_a_note_says.

Grade "must", not "should": this is silent loss of the person's own edit, or a deleted note coming back, under the expected load: the person works in Notes while a sync runs, often having just pressed F5 in Notes.

STANDS: The race is real at 0b781473. The notes sync runs on a worker thread with its own database connection (wx_app.rs:32802). The editor's Save writes on the window's own connection (wx_app.rs:3048, the_person_changed_the_note sets pending = 1). Nothing stops a Save while a sync is running: ASyncUnderWay only blocks undo.

take_what_has_arrived reads every note once (notes_sync.rs:740) and then waits on the network for each changed note (790). It checks the waiting flag on that old copy (843-844). write_it_down then upserts the whole row with pending false (898). save_note is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (notes.rs:326-343), so a row deleted by a move or a delete comes back.

So an edit saved in that gap is lost and never sent, but only when the backend's copy of the same note also changed. If it did not, the marker check skips the note, or the titles match and the guarded a_backend_took_the_note path runs. Nothing ledgers this read-side gap, and the changelog entry at line 1690 says a note edited "while it syncs is kept and sent", which overclaims.

"should" is the honest group, not "must". Notes sync only runs when the person presses F5 or Sync Now in Notes (sync_the_module, wx_app.rs:32428). Loss needs the same note edited on another device and saved here within the few seconds of that sync's fetches. That is a real but rare silent loss of one edit, not a break at the expected load.

The first proposed fix is wrong for the move and delete cases. `ours.and_then(|n| cache.get_note(&n.id).ok().flatten())` turns a vanished row into None, and write_it_down's None arm then makes a brand-new note with a fresh id. So the moved or deleted note still comes back, under a new id, and the finding's claim "a removed row is not made again" is false.

Smallest fix that works: after the fetch, re-read by id. If the row is gone, `continue`. If it is pending and differs, hold the conflict. Otherwise write. Better still, do the re-read and the write in one immediate transaction, the way a_backend_took_the_note now does. Alternatively, write through a dedicated `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND updated_at = ?` rather than the upsert.

Missing test: give the Scripted service a `meanwhile` hook in what_a_note_says, like the one 13.2-20 added for written, so this case has a test that fails.

findings.title: Mail left out when an archive is first looked over is never mentioned
findings.what_this_is: Before importing, the program looks over every entry in the chosen zip or folder. It reads up to 64 KB of each entry. An entry that fails at this point is left out of the import and only counted. Reasons include damage, a size that lies, encryption, or a folder nested too deep.
findings.problem: Outside tests, nothing reads that count. `how_many_could_not_be_read` and `how_many_were_too_deep_to_follow` are called only by mailbox_archive's own tests. The closing sentence is built from `what_it_holds()` alone, so these entries vanish without a word. Plan 13.2-31.7 added a `did_not_match` count to that look-over, but only `nothing_at_all` reads it. Plan 13.2-31.8 reports the same fault only when it shows up later, during the piece-by-piece read. The archive's own doc comment says reporting this count "is the caller's job", and no caller does it.
findings.concrete_case: Take the fixture from 13.2-31.8's end-to-end test: Altered.mbox with 2,000 messages, plus Honest.mbox with 3. Record Altered's size as 10,000 bytes instead of 100,000. The look-over reads 64 KB, and zip 9.0.4 fails the read once it passes 10,000 bytes. Altered is dropped, and the import says only "Imported 1 folder, 3 messages." A second case: a zip of 500 small .eml files with one of them damaged gives "Imported 1 folder, 499 messages." and nothing more. Someone who trusts that sentence may delete the archive.
findings.fix: In `an_archive_brought_in`, right after `opened(at)`, fold the archive's counts into `counted`. Add the did-not-match count (one small getter) to `did_not_match_and_none_came_in`, which already has its sentence. Put the remaining unreadable entries and the too-deep count into one new sentence, for example "N files in the archive could not be read and were left out". Add one end-to-end case with a recorded size under 64 KB.
findings.if_we_skip: An import that left whole folders or messages behind reports itself as complete. Only the log knows.
findings.evidence: `git grep -n 'how_many_could_not_be_read\|how_many_were_too_deep_to_follow' 0b781473 -- src tests`: only mailbox_archive.rs tests (L1829, L2661, L2672, L2713). The same grep at 2a4679a9 shows no caller there either. importing_messages.rs L1034: `let plan = import_tree::where_the_folders_land(&archive.what_it_holds());`. import_tree.rs L434: `where_the_folders_land(entries: &[EntryInTheArchive])` sees only the kept entries. mailbox_archive.rs L405-411: a `how_it_begins` error goes to `one_could_not_be_read` and is never pushed. L588-599: `did_not_match` is read only when `entries` is empty. import_tree.rs L112: `ENOUGH_TO_TELL_WHAT_IT_HOLDS = 64 * 1024`. zip-9.0.4 src/crc32.rs L45-48: InvalidData once more bytes than declared are read. No open ledger row in .planning/WINDOWS.md names these counts.
checker_notes:
STANDS: The finding holds: I walked the code at 0b781473 and the wrong closing sentence really happens. In mailbox_archive.rs, a_zip_looked_over (L362-411) reads the first 64 KB of each entry. If that read fails (L404-409), or by_index fails (L363-371, for example on an encrypted entry), the entry goes to one_could_not_be_read. That function only counts it and writes a log line (L573-579), so the entry never reaches `entries`. nothing_at_all (L588-599) looks at the counts only when `entries` is empty. MailboxArchive::of copies could_not_be_read and too_deep_to_follow onto the archive but drops did_not_match (L794-795). The two getters (L805-812) say in their own doc comment that reporting the count "is the caller's job". `git grep` finds them called only in mailbox_archive's own tests (L1829, L2661, L2672, L2713).

an_archive_brought_in (importing_messages.rs L1030-1096) is the only real caller. It is reached from wx_app.rs L17170, which returns its string unchanged. It builds the plan from archive.what_it_holds() alone and never reads either count. FoldersImported::could_not_be_read is overwritten by carry_the_mail_counts from MessagesImported (import_tree.rs L393), so it never carries the look-over count. what_the_folder_import_did (L519-589) has no sentence for it.

Concrete reproduction from the repo's own fixtures:
1. The test at mailbox_archive.rs L1805 stores Work/Broken.mbox, small and with one byte damaged. Its CRC (checksum) check fails at end of file inside the 64 KB read. The archive opens with Invoices.mbox and one.eml only, and how_many_could_not_be_read() == 1. Fed to an_archive_brought_in, it says "Imported 2 folders, N messages." with no word about Broken.mbox.
2. The finding's lying-size case also holds. The tests use a_zip_recording_altered_as at 100,000 and 300,000 bytes, which goes through the piece-by-piece path. At 10,000, below 64 KB, the look-over itself fails: zip 9.0.4's Crc32Reader::count (crc32.rs L45-48) gives InvalidData once more bytes than the recorded size are read. Altered.mbox is dropped silently, and only "Imported 1 folder, 3 messages." is said.

Phase 13.2 made this worse. At 2a4679a9 the lock file had zip 7.2.0, whose crc32.rs has no size limit. The 13.2-31.7 move to 9.0.4 turned recorded sizes under 64 KB into a new silent drop at look-over. Ledger 906's fix covers only "64 KB recorded or more".

No ledger row in .planning/WINDOWS.md and no changelog entry states this limitation. The changelog's "goes to the log and no further" note is about calendar syncs. So this is a wrong result at the head commit: an import that left mail in the archive reports itself as complete.

STANDS: The finding holds at 0b781473, and nothing at the head commit covers it.

1. **No caller reads the counts.** At the head commit, `how_many_could_not_be_read` and `how_many_were_too_deep_to_follow` are called only from mailbox_archive's own tests. The test at L1805-1829 even proves the drop: a zip with a damaged Work/Broken.mbox next to two good entries opens, keeps only the good two, and counts 1.

2. **The import never says it.** `an_archive_brought_in` (L1030-1096) builds its sentence from `where_the_folders_land(&archive.what_it_holds())`, which sees only the kept entries, plus the mail counts. The only real caller, wx_app.rs:17170, returns that sentence unchanged. `FoldersImported` has no field for these counts.

3. **What 13.2 did and did not cover.** 13.2-31.7 added `did_not_match`, but only `nothing_at_all` reads it, so its sentence speaks only when every entry fails. 13.2-31.8's own premise 1 says "Under 64 KB recorded the look-over refuses the entry and 13.2-31.7's sentence speaks." That is wrong whenever a good entry sits beside the damaged one.

4. **The zip 9.0.4 move made it worse.** On zip 7.2.0 an entry that records a size under 64 KB, smaller than its real contents, was read whole and its mail came in (31.7 premise 6). On 9.0.4 the first 64 KB read, which looks over each entry before the import, fails with InvalidData. The entry is then dropped and never mentioned, so a mixed archive says only "Imported 1 folder, 3 messages."

5. **No changelog line or ledger row covers it.**
   - The changelog entries for 31.7 and 31.8 talk only about a zip that is wholly damaged and about stops during the piece-by-piece read.
   - Ledger row 905 is a test for the tester to listen to; its zip has only one entry.
   - Ledger 908 covers other stops during the piece-by-piece read, not entries dropped when the archive is first looked over.
   - The gap was raised in phase 4.2's sweep (.planning/sweeps/logic-layers.md section 9, PLANS-README L401-415) and handed to phase 7. Phase 7's plans never mention it, and it has no WINDOWS.md row.
   - The comment at mailbox_archive.rs L446-449 says a folder that is too deep "is never left behind in silence". It is.

6. **Is the fix safe?** It touches only the sentence and `FoldersImported`. One change to the wording: an entry dropped while the archive is looked over can be a single .eml or .msg file, so do not fold it into the "mailbox file" sentence. Use one sentence about files instead. The Outlook data file import already has one to copy (importing_an_outlook_data_file.rs:402, "N things in the file could not be read and were left in it").

7. **Group: must.** The import reports itself complete while folders or messages stay behind in the archive. For the size case this is a regression the zip move brought in.

STANDS: Confirmed at 0b781473. When the import first looks over a zip or folder (`a_zip_looked_over` and `walked`, mailbox_archive.rs L402-410, L616-688), it reads up to 64 KB of each entry. An entry that fails there goes to `one_could_not_be_read` and is never added to `entries`. `nothing_at_all` (L588-599) only speaks when no entry was kept at all. `MailboxArchive::of` keeps `could_not_be_read` and `too_deep_to_follow` but drops `did_not_match`. The only callers of `how_many_could_not_be_read` and `how_many_were_too_deep_to_follow` are tests (L1829, L2661, L2672, L2713). The real import, `an_archive_brought_in` (importing_messages.rs L1022-1096), runs from wx_app.rs L17170. It builds its sentence from `what_it_holds()`, and `FoldersImported` (import_tree.rs L347-382) has no field for these entries, so `what_the_folder_import_did` cannot say them.

The test `test_one_entry_that_cannot_be_read_does_not_take_the_rest_of_the_archive_with_it` (mailbox_archive.rs L1805) builds exactly the second case: one damaged entry in a zip next to good ones. It opens, the count is 1, and the import's closing sentence never mentions it. The first case also holds. In zip 9.0.4, `Crc32Reader::count` fails with InvalidData once more bytes come out than the recorded size, so an entry recorded under 64 KB fails during the look-over and is dropped without a word.

13.2 touched this flow and claimed it was covered. 13.2-31.8-PLAN.md L91 says "Under 64 KB recorded the look-over refuses the entry and 13.2-31.7's sentence speaks". That is only true when the bad entry is the only one in the archive. The gap is also known and was never closed. `.planning/sweeps/logic-layers.md` §9 and the phase 04.2 README handed it to phase 7, the archive's own doc comment says reporting the count is "the caller's job", and no row in WINDOWS.md or the changelog states the limit. So it is neither a decided limit nor a ledgered one.

On the lens: damaged archives are rare for one person on a desktop. Even so, the result is a wrong closing sentence: it reports a complete import while whole mailbox files were left behind, and that sentence is what someone reads before deleting the archive. That is a bug, so "must" fits the brief.

The proposed fix works and is close to the smallest. The minimum is one field on `FoldersImported`, filled right after `opened(at)` from the two existing getters, plus one sentence such as "N files in the archive could not be read and were left out". The `did_not_match` getter, which would route these entries to the existing "damaged or changed" sentence, is optional polish. If it is added, subtract that count from the could-not-be-read count, because it is a subset, so no entry is reported twice.

findings.title: Conversation row stays after some deletes and moves
findings.what_this_is: bring_the_conversation_rows_up_to_date is 13.2-02's catch-up: after a change made here, it updates the conversation rows on screen at once. It finds which conversations were touched with conversations_holding, which reads each message's thread_id and account from the store after the change.
findings.problem: Two changes erase that information before it is read. take_off_this_computer rewrites the row without thread_id, because KEPT_WHEN_TAKEN_OFF does not list it, so conversations_holding finds nothing and the catch-up returns early. A move to another account puts the row in the other account's folder, so the read names the other account's conversation, which matches no row on screen.
findings.concrete_case: Conversation view on a POP account's Trash, or Shift+Delete in any POP folder or folder on this computer: press Delete on a conversation row. local_delete::perform calls take_off_this_computer, then MessageLeftTheFolder reaches take_row_out_of_the_list and the catch-up, but conversations_holding([id]) is empty, so the row stays until the folder is read again. Likewise, moving a message or a conversation into another account's folder leaves the source row showing its old count. This is the owner's "Delete shows only after the next sync" report, still open on these paths.
findings.fix: Read the conversations before the change. Call conversations_holding when the set is remembered (the_set_leaving, and the single-message path), keep the result on ASetLeaving, and give those names to the catch-up instead of reading them after the write. Add cases for take_off_this_computer and for a move across accounts.
findings.if_we_skip: Screen reader users on POP or local folders, or moving mail between accounts, hear the delete or move confirmed while the row stays. That is the regression the phase set out to fix.
findings.evidence: git show 0b781473:src/presentation/wx_app.rs L28071-28119: `match cache.conversations_holding(touched) { Ok(named) if named.is_empty() => return, ...}`. git show 0b781473:src/data/message_cache/messages.rs L2707-2730 filters `m.thread_id IS NOT NULL AND m.thread_id <> ''` and takes the account from the current folder. git show 0b781473:src/data/message_cache/taken_off_this_computer.rs L38-60: KEPT_WHEN_TAKEN_OFF has no thread_id, and L233-255 deletes and writes the row back. mod.rs L3253 adds thread_id as TEXT with no default. local_delete.rs RemoveFromThisComputer calls take_off_this_computer. moves_waiting.rs (application) L375-378 moves a crossing's row into the other account's folder. conversations.rs WhoseConversation::is matches account and thread. tests/a_change_made_here_reaches_the_conversation_rows.rs L261-274 tests only delete_message, which keeps thread_id.
checker_notes: STANDS: The bug is real at 0b781473. Path for a POP Inbox in conversation view with Shift+Delete, or Delete in a POP Trash. The Delete arm (wx_app.rs L5754-5770) calls delete_these. That calls delete_if_local (L28341), which runs local_delete::perform. Because local_folders::deleting answers RemoveFromThisComputer for Deleting::Outright or for the Trash, perform calls take_off_this_computer. That runs on the UI thread before MessageLeftTheFolder is sent. take_off_this_computer deletes the row and writes it back with only KEPT_WHEN_TAKEN_OFF (id, folder_id, uid, pop_uidl, downloaded_at, filed_here, original_uid, original_account_id) plus deleted=1. thread_id is a nullable TEXT column (mod.rs L3253), so it comes back NULL. The MessageLeftTheFolder arm (L25181) calls take_row_out_of_the_list. Under conversation view that calls bring_the_conversation_rows_up_to_date with the message ids, for one message or once for the last of a set. conversations_holding filters `m.thread_id IS NOT NULL AND <> ''`, so it returns nothing and the catch-up returns early at `Ok(named) if named.is_empty() => return`. Nothing else refreshes the rows: FolderCountsMoved only rewords the folder tree. So the conversation row stays until the folder is read again. POP messages do have a thread_id (upsert sets it at messages.rs L1363), so their conversation rows exist. The cross-account half also holds. moves_waiting::what_happens_here moves the row into the other account's folder. Then complete_here_then_tell_the_server calls take_row_out_of_the_list. conversations_holding names the conversation under the destination account (it reads f.account_id), and WhoseConversation::is needs both account and thread to match. So view_state::bring_rows_up_to_date leaves the source account's row unchanged. The test file only covers delete_message, which keeps thread_id. It has no case for take_off_this_computer or for a move across accounts. Reading the conversations before the write, as the finding proposes, would fix both.

STANDS: I could not refute this. Both paths are real at 0b781473 and nothing in the tree covers them.

1. **Taking a message off this computer.** `take_off_this_computer` deletes the row and writes it back with only `KEPT_WHEN_TAKEN_OFF` (taken_off_this_computer.rs L38-60, L233-255). That list leaves out `thread_id`, which mod.rs L3253 adds as a plain TEXT column, and no trigger sets it again. So the row comes back with no `thread_id`.
   - Delete in a POP or local Trash, or Shift+Delete in any local folder, reaches `LocalDelete::RemoveFromThisComputer` (local_folders.rs L302-309).

2. **Moving into another account.** `what_happens_here` moves the row into the other account's folder (moves_waiting.rs L375-377) before `take_row_out_of_the_list` runs (wx_app.rs L26865).

1. A Delete under conversation view runs delete_these, then delete_if_local, then local_delete::perform. That sends MessageLeftTheFolder, which runs take_row_out_of_the_list (wx_app.rs L25181) and then the catch-up. Nothing else reloads the list: the FolderCountsMoved handler only rewords the folder tree.

2. The catch-up finds the touched conversations with conversations_holding (messages.rs L2707) after the write. That query skips rows with no thread_id and takes the account from the folder the message is in now.
